gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v5cbd42dbf1.matiz: After a country name it's read じん: 日本人 (a Japanese person). On its own, “person”, it's ひと. The very polite word is 方 (かた).

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v3906cbce2e.matiz: For something near the listener. It also points back to what the other person just said, where English would use **that** or **it**: “that thing you mentioned”.
v3906cbce2e.mnemo: “**So**, what's **that** you've got?” The こそあど family: **そ** is near you. それ = **that** thing by you.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v98163e1740.frase: ニャンは日本の猫です。
v98163e1740.frase_furigana: ニャンは日本[にほん]の 猫[ねこ]です。
v98163e1740.frase_es: Nyan is a cat from Japan.

gramatica.nota: の joins two nouns: 日本の猫 = “a cat from Japan”, “a Japanese cat”.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v98163e1740.matiz: Also read にっぽん, which sounds more emphatic (sports, stamps, banknotes). 日本人 = a Japanese person; 日本語 = the Japanese language.

vf68273d21f.frase: 私の名前はニャンです。
vf68273d21f.frase_furigana: 私[わたし]の名前[なまえ]はニャンです。

gramatica.nota: 私の名前 = “my name”: the owner comes before の, like English 's.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vf68273d21f.matiz: When it's someone else's name, add お for respect: お名前は? (What's your name?)

v534b796a04.matiz: Casual, between friends. The polite version is ありがとうございます.

vca5c6a1e7a.frase: ニャンは先生じゃないです。
vca5c6a1e7a.frase_furigana: ニャンは先生[せんせい]じゃないです。

gramatica.nota: じゃないです is the negative of です: “is not”.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vca5c6a1e7a.matiz: Also a respectful title for doctors, lawyers, writers and other experts: 田中先生 (Dr. Tanaka, Mr. Tanaka). Students say 先生 where English would say “you” or “Sir/Miss”. You never use it about yourself.

vac475c12cc.frase: ニャンは私の友達です。
vac475c12cc.frase_furigana: ニャンは 私[わたし]の友達[ともだち]です。
vac475c12cc.tono: トモダチ

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vac475c12cc.matiz: 達 was originally a plural ending, but 友達 works fine for just one friend.

v6e9eadcff2.frase_furigana: それは誰[だれ]の 本[ほん]ですか。

gramatica.nota: 誰の = “whose”: の after 誰 works like English 's.

v6e9eadcff2.matiz: Polite version: どなた. 誰か = someone; 誰も + a negative verb = nobody.

v3a987a1b0b.frase: それは何のことですか。
v3a987a1b0b.frase_furigana: それは 何[なん]のことですか。
v3a987a1b0b.matiz: An abstract “thing”: a matter, fact, event or idea. English uses “thing” for everything, but a physical object is 物 (もの). こと is usually written in kana.

vd7c45d9e06.frase_furigana: あなたも 先生[せんせい]ですか。

gramatica.nota: も replaces は and adds “too / also”.

vd7c45d9e06.matiz: Can sound distant or even rude. The natural way is to use the person's name with さん, even to their face: “Is Tanaka-san coming?” rather than “Are you coming?”. Wives traditionally use あなた to mean “dear”.
vd7c45d9e06.mnemo: A waiter pulls out a chair: “**An' a ta**ble for **you**?” あなた = **you**.

v7f544e908d.frase: ニャンは何を見ますか。
v7f544e908d.frase_furigana: ニャンは 何[なに]を見[み]ますか。

gramatica.nota: を marks what is looked at, eaten, read…: the direct object.

v7f544e908d.matiz: A る-verb: 見ます, 見ない, 見て. 見て on its own = Look! One verb covers see, look and watch: テレビを見る = to watch TV.

v45b8269237.frase: ニャンは何を食べますか。
v45b8269237.frase_furigana: ニャンは 何[なに]を食[た]べますか。

gramatica.nota: 食べます is the polite form of 食べる.

v45b8269237.matiz: A る-verb: 食べます, 食べない, 食べて.

v8470accbc2.frase_es: What are you going to do?
v8470accbc2.matiz: Irregular. It sticks to lots of nouns to make verbs: 勉強する (to study), 心配する (to worry). Sports and games use する where English says “play”: テニスをする.

vbe7c961dc1.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]は 何[なに]を飲[の]みますか。
vbe7c961dc1.matiz: Also used for taking medicine, where English says “take”: 薬を飲む. With no object it often means drinking alcohol: 飲みに行く = to go out for drinks.

vab02168390.frase_furigana: 私[わたし]は 本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vab02168390.matiz: Also used for how kanji are read: この 漢字[かんじ]はどう 読[よ]みますか = How do you read this kanji?

v0d61532641.frase_furigana: 名前[なまえ]を書[か]きます。
v0d61532641.matiz: Drawing or painting is also かく, but with a different kanji: 描[か]く.

ve3d391e7fb.frase: ニャンは水を飲みます。
ve3d391e7fb.frase_furigana: ニャンは水[みず]を 飲[の]みます。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

ve3d391e7fb.matiz: Only cold or room-temperature water. Hot water has its own word: お湯. So where English says “hot water”, Japanese just says お湯.

vbac3d64292.frase: ニャンはおにぎりを食べます。
vbac3d64292.frase_furigana: ニャンはおにぎりを 食[た]べます。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vbac3d64292.matiz: Rice pressed into a triangle, often wrapped in seaweed with a filling inside. Nyan's favorite food.

ve511de41c7.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん]に 猫[ねこ]がいます。

gramatica.nota: いる means “there is / to be somewhere” for living things; に marks where.
gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
が: who or what (the identified subject)
に: destination, time, where something is

ve511de41c7.matiz: いる for people and animals; ある for objects and plants. Having family is said the same way: 兄がいる = I have an older brother (literally, “there is an older brother”).
ve511de41c7.mnemo: An **ee**l wriggles on its own: いる (**ee**-ru) is for things that move by themselves. Things that just sit there use ある.

v3d7f9ddbe3.frase: すみません、それは私の本です。
v3d7f9ddbe3.frase_furigana: すみません、それは 私[わたし]の 本[ほん]です。
v3d7f9ddbe3.tono: スミマセン

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v3d7f9ddbe3.matiz: Sorry, excuse me (to call a waiter or get someone's attention), and even “thank you” when someone has gone to trouble for you. Japanese often apologizes where English would thank.
v3d7f9ddbe3.mnemo: “**Sue me**, man… **sorry**!” すみません (**sumi**masen) = **excuse me / sorry**.

gramatica.nota: ある means “there is / to be somewhere” for things.
gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v0f5e1d8c2e.matiz: Its negative is ない, not “あらない”: a one-off. It's also how you say you “have” things: 時間がある = I have time.
v0f5e1d8c2e.mnemo: Picture an **ar**mchair: it just sits there. ある (**a**ru) is for things that don't move by themselves. Living things use いる.

v746a980bee.frase: ニャンは日本に行きます。
v746a980bee.frase_furigana: ニャンは 日本[にほん]に行[い]きます。

gramatica.nota: に marks where you're going.
gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is
は: the topic of the sentence

v746a980bee.matiz: Irregular て-form: 行って (not “行いて”). Careful: when you head over to the person you're talking to, Japanese uses 行く where English says “come”: 今行く! = I'm coming!

vd0e3513b33.frase_furigana: 友達[ともだち]が来[き]ます。

gramatica.nota: が points out who does the action when it's new information.
gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

vd0e3513b33.matiz: Movement toward where the speaker is. If you're going over to someone else, it's 行く, even when English would say “I'll come to your place”.
vd0e3513b33.mnemo: Three faces of one verb: **ku**ru, **ki**masu, **ko**nai. The vowel changes, the kanji stays.

v60a62ace27.frase: ニャンはここにいます。
v60a62ace27.frase_furigana: ニャンはここにいます。

gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v60a62ace27.mnemo: The こそあど family: **こ** is **c**lose to me. ここ = **here**, right where I am.

vd7de52a7ff.frase_furigana: 私[わたし]の 本[ほん]はどこですか。
vd7de52a7ff.mnemo: The こそあど family: **ど** asks. “**Do** you know **where**?” どこ = **where?**

vabe6f3d928.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]は家[いえ]にいます。

gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

vabe6f3d928.matiz: Also read うち, which feels warmer: “my home, my family”. いえ sounds more like the building, a bit like house vs. home in English.

v3b5d947a91.frase_furigana: いい 名前[なまえ]ですね。

gramatica.nota: ね at the end invites agreement, like “isn't it?”.
gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v3b5d947a91.matiz: Irregular: its negative and past come from the older form よい: よくない, よかった. Never “いくない”. Watch out: いいです can also be a polite “no thanks”, like English “I'm good”.
v3b5d947a91.mnemo: Two thumbs up, side by side: い い. All **good**!

vd5c8899733.frase: ニャンはおにぎりが好きです。
vd5c8899733.frase_furigana: ニャンはおにぎりが好[す]きです。

gramatica.nota: What you like takes が: おにぎりが好き.
gramatica.titulo: Liking and being good at: が with adjectives
が: who or what (the identified subject)

vd5c8899733.matiz: It's a な-adjective, not a verb: literally “onigiri is likable (to Nyan)”. Said to a person (あなたが好き) it's usually a confession: “I like you” in the romantic sense.

v2ccea33000.frase_furigana: ニャンは眠[ねむ]いです。

gramatica.nota: い-adjectives go straight before です.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v856c880784.frase_furigana: 大[おお]きい 猫[ねこ]ですね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v856c880784.matiz: Before a noun, both 大きい and 大きな work. To end a sentence (“it's big”), only 大きい.

vbeceac4629.frase: ニャンも学校に行きます。
vbeceac4629.frase_furigana: ニャンも学校[がっこう]に 行[い]きます。
vbeceac4629.tono: ガッコウ

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v66b6e11279.frase_furigana: それは高[たか]いですか。
v66b6e11279.matiz: Works for price and for height: a 高い building is tall, a 高い ring is expensive. For a tall person, say 背が高い.

va375891d36.frase_furigana: 新[あたら]しい 本[ほん]ですね。
va375891d36.tono: アタラシイ

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

va375891d36.matiz: For fresh food, Japanese prefers 新鮮[しんせん]: 新鮮[しんせん]な 魚[さかな] (fresh fish).

vf17ca3c033.frase_furigana: ここに 水[みず]がないです。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
に: destination, time, where something is

vf17ca3c033.matiz: The negative of ある, and it behaves like an い-adjective (past: 無かった). Almost always written in kana: ない.

v9f2a076b5d.frase_furigana: この 猫[ねこ]は 私[わたし]の 友達[ともだち]です。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v9f2a076b5d.matiz: Never stands alone: この needs a noun after it (この本, this book). On its own, “this one” is これ.
v9f2a076b5d.mnemo: The こそあど family: **こ** is **c**lose to me. この + noun: この本 = **this** book.

ve5ee0c1d9d.frase: このおにぎりはおいしいです。
ve5ee0c1d9d.frase_furigana: このおにぎりはおいしいです。
ve5ee0c1d9d.tono: オイシイ

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

ve5ee0c1d9d.matiz: Usually written in kana: おいしい. A more casual, masculine word is うまい; the opposite is まずい. Japanese say it much more often than English says “delicious”: it's the everyday “this is good”.
ve5ee0c1d9d.mnemo: Take a bite and shout: “**Oi**, **see**? So **delicious**!” (Its kanji 美味しい = beauty 美 + flavor 味.)

v5ddd971b47.tono: ハジメマシテ
v5ddd971b47.frase_es: Nice to meet you, I'm Nyan.
v5ddd971b47.matiz: Only the very first time you meet someone. It literally means “for the first time”, so it opens the introduction; the usual closing line is よろしくお願いします.

v41fe4e403b.frase_furigana: それは本当[ほんとう]ですか。
v41fe4e403b.tono: ホントウ

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v41fe4e403b.matiz: 本当に = really, truly. Casual: ほんと. On its own, ほんと? works like “Really?”.

v99990e6825.frase_furigana: 学校[がっこう]で勉強[べんきょう]します。
v99990e6825.tono: ベンキョウ

gramatica.nota: で marks where an action happens (に marks where something simply is).
gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v99990e6825.matiz: It's a noun; add する and it becomes a verb: 勉強する, to study. It feels like work: homework, exams, cramming.

v7f225cb103.frase: ニャンと日本語を勉強します。
v7f225cb103.frase_furigana: ニャンと日本[にほん] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう]します。
v7f225cb103.tono: ニホンゴ

gramatica.nota: と = “with” (someone).
gramatica.titulo: と and や: lists of things

v7f225cb103.matiz: 語 after a country name gives its language: 英語 (English), フランス語 (French). In English “Japanese” is both the language and the people; in Japanese the person is 日本人.

v3867855b87.tono: ヨロシク

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v3867855b87.matiz: Said when you introduce yourself or ask a favor: roughly “please be good to me”. English has no single equivalent; “nice to meet you”, “thanks in advance” and “best regards” each cover part of it. Polite version: よろしくお願いします.

v4834e82ff7.frase: ニャンは漢字を書きます。
v4834e82ff7.frase_furigana: ニャンは漢字[かんじ]を 書[か]きます。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vbb1f0fe910.frase: 日本語がわかりますか。
vbb1f0fe910.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]がわかりますか。

gramatica.nota: With わかる, the thing understood takes が, not を.
gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

vbb1f0fe910.matiz: What you understand takes が: 日本語が分かる. Also written with kanji: 分かる. わかった! is the everyday “Got it!” or “OK!”.

v513bf6fe63.frase: ニャンは何ができますか。
v513bf6fe63.frase_furigana: ニャンは 何[なに]ができますか。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v513bf6fe63.matiz: Also “to be finished, be ready”: ご飯ができた = Dinner's ready! What you can do takes が. Often written in kana.

vc6db0d793a.frase_furigana: 今日[きょう]は 学校[がっこう]に 行[い]きます。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is
は: the topic of the sentence

vc6db0d793a.matiz: No に after it. The greeting こんにちは comes from 今日は, “as for today…”.
vc6db0d793a.mnemo: You're off to **Kyo**to **today**: きょう. A special reading that doesn't come from its kanji.

v6b7cbce367.frase_furigana: 明日[あした]も 勉強[べんきょう]します。
v6b7cbce367.matiz: More formal: あす. Very formal: みょうにち. No に after it.
v6b7cbce367.mnemo: “**Ah, she ta**kes the test **tomorrow**!” あした = **tomorrow**. A special reading that doesn't come from its kanji.

v49bec87abb.frase: ニャンは「おにぎり」って言う。
v49bec87abb.frase_furigana: ニャンは「おにぎり」って言[ゆ]う。

gramatica.nota: って is the spoken, casual form of と: it marks what is said.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
は: the topic of the sentence

v49bec87abb.matiz: Written いう but pronounced “yuu”. て-form: 言って.

v01a0c6ed9c.frase_furigana: ニャンは 先生[せんせい]になる。
v01a0c6ed9c.frase_es: Nyan is going to be a teacher.

gramatica.nota: 〜になる = “to become”. Among friends: なる instead of なります.
gramatica.titulo: になる (to become) and にする (to decide, to make)
Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
は: the topic of the sentence

v01a0c6ed9c.matiz: Very versatile: a change of state, a result, “to end up”. With い-adjectives it uses く: 高くなる (to get expensive). It's often where English says “get”: 寒くなる = to get cold.
v01a0c6ed9c.mnemo: **Naru**to's dream is to **become** Hokage. なる = **to become**.

v19216562af.frase_furigana: その 本[ほん]、 高[たか]いね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v19216562af.matiz: Always comes before a noun. On its own, with nothing after it, it's それ.
v19216562af.mnemo: The こそあど family: **そ** is near you. その + noun: その本 = **that** book (by you).

v5b0c9ef6aa.frase: おいしいものが好きです。
v5b0c9ef6aa.frase_furigana: おいしいものが 好[す]きです。

gramatica.titulo: Liking and being good at: が with adjectives

v5b0c9ef6aa.matiz: Physical objects. For matters, facts or ideas, use こと. English “thing” covers both, so keep them apart: 好きなもの = things you like (objects, food); 好きなこと = things you like doing.

v8c44c3b4cf.frase: ニャンはいい猫だと思う。
v8c44c3b4cf.frase_furigana: ニャンはいい 猫[ねこ]だと思[おも]う。
v8c44c3b4cf.frase_es: I think Nyan is a good cat.

gramatica.nota: 〜と思う = “I think that…”; the part before it is in plain form (だ, not です). Among friends, 思う instead of 思います.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v8c44c3b4cf.matiz: For opinions and feelings: “I think, it seems to me”. 考える is reasoning, thinking something through.

vd17aa56d37.frase_furigana: ニャン、 日本[にほん]はどう?

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vd17aa56d37.matiz: Careful: “What do you think?” is どう思う (literally “how do you think?”), not “何を思う”. どうですか = How is it? / How about it?
vd17aa56d37.mnemo: どう sounds like **dough**: “**How** do you make **dough**?” (The こそあど family: **ど** asks the question.)

ve699b96a8e.frase_furigana: 二[に] 時[じ]に 学校[がっこう]に 行[い]きます。
ve699b96a8e.frase_es: I go to school at two.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

ve699b96a8e.matiz: With native Japanese counters: 二つ (ふたつ), 二人 (ふたり).

v65cd46e7b9.frase_furigana: 自分[じぶん]の 名前[なまえ]を 書[か]く。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v65cd46e7b9.matiz: Can refer to anyone depending on context: myself, yourself, himself. 自分で = by yourself. In the Kansai area it can also mean “you”.

vaa5cc8f107.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]は 私[わたし]の 友達[ともだち]です。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vaa5cc8f107.matiz: Also means “boyfriend” (彼氏 is clearer). In conversation people prefer to use the person's name, so 彼 comes up much less than English “he”.

v0e9223b20b.frase_furigana: 明日[あした]、 何[なに]をやる?

gramatica.nota: Among friends, the dictionary form alone works as a question: やる? instead of やりますか.
gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v0e9223b20b.matiz: Like する, but more casual and energetic. It can also mean “to give” to animals or plants: 猫にえさをやる = to feed the cat.
v0e9223b20b.mnemo: “**Yah**! Let's **do** it!” やる = **to do**, with more punch than する.

vae9edd5db6.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]らは 私[わたし]の 友達[ともだち]だ。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v7cf28dc9bd.matiz: No に after it. 今日 (today) and 今年 (this year) use the same kanji with a different reading.

vbfe4d8728f.tono: オハヨウ
vbfe4d8728f.matiz: With people you don't know well or your boss: おはようございます.

v316aa46487.frase: 日本はいいところだよ。
v316aa46487.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん]はいいところだよ。
v316aa46487.frase_es: Japan is a great place, you know.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v316aa46487.matiz: Very flexible: place, part, point, moment. In kanji, 所. 私のところ = my place.
v316aa46487.mnemo: **To**kyo, **Co**rk, **Ro**me: ところ (**to-ko-ro**) is any **place** at all.

v7873538a47.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]は 家[いえ]の中[なか]にいます。
v7873538a47.frase_es: The cat is inside the house.

gramatica.nota: X の中 = “inside X”.

gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v7873538a47.matiz: Also “in the middle of, among”: 雨の中 = out in the rain.

v52b63d9bde.frase: 三時間ぐらい日本語の勉強をする。
v52b63d9bde.frase_furigana: 三[さん] 時間[じかん]ぐらい 日本[にほん] 語[ご]の 勉強[べんきょう]をする。
v52b63d9bde.frase_es: I study Japanese for about three hours.

gramatica.nota: ぐらい / くらい after a number = “about”: 三時間ぐらい.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v52b63d9bde.matiz: Three things: 三つ (みっつ). Sometimes it changes the sound of what follows: 三本 = さんぼん.

v1fc6718229.frase: 学校の前に猫がいます。
v1fc6718229.frase_furigana: 学校[がっこう]の前[まえ]に 猫[ねこ]がいます。
v1fc6718229.frase_es: There's a cat in front of the school.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v1fc6718229.matiz: In space, “in front”; in time, “before”: 三年前 = three years ago. Like English “ago”, it comes after the time.

va92c1b7318.matiz: After a て-form it asks for an action: 待ってください = please wait. After a thing + を, it asks for that thing.
va92c1b7318.mnemo: Hand out at the counter: “**Could a** **sigh** get me one? **Please**?” く・だ・さい ≈ **koo-da-sigh** = **please**.

vbc9988f90d.frase: いいえ、私は先生じゃないです。
vbc9988f90d.frase_furigana: いいえ、 私[わたし]は 先生[せんせい]じゃないです。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vbc9988f90d.matiz: Sounds rather blunt, so people often soften it or avoid it. It also brushes things off: after a “thank you”, いいえ = “not at all, you're welcome”.
vbc9988f90d.mnemo: Shake your head side to side: “**Eee**… **eh**… **no**.” いいえ = **no**.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vd669529e98.matiz: そうですか = Oh, really? / I see; そうです = That's right; そうですね = Yes, I suppose so (also a thinking pause, like “Let's see…”).
vd669529e98.mnemo: “**So** you say!” The こそあど family: **そ** is near you. そう = **like that**, the way you said it.

v78e514e895.frase_furigana: 今日[きょう]は時間[じかん]ある?

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
は: the topic of the sentence

v78e514e895.matiz: Time as an amount, and also “hours”: 二時間 = two hours. Time on the clock uses 時: 三時 = three o'clock.

v45a74b3626.frase_furigana: 私[わたし]は知[し]りません。

gramatica.nota: 知りません: the polite negative ends in ません.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v45a74b3626.matiz: Strictly it means “to come to know”, so “I know” is almost always 知っています (ている form). But “I don't know” is 知りません, without ている.

v8fc35eef5b.frase_furigana: 二[に] 時[じ]に 家[いえ]を出[で]る。

gramatica.nota: With 出る, the place you leave takes を.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v8fc35eef5b.matiz: Intransitive: you are the one going out. Taking something out is 出す. Also “to appear”: テレビに出る = to be on TV.

v27191c19d7.frase_furigana: ニャンはもう 食[た]べた。

gramatica.nota: た is the plain past. Among friends: もう食べた instead of もう食べました.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v27191c19d7.matiz: With a negative it means “not anymore”: もう食べない = I'm not eating any more. もういい = That's enough. It also means “more”: もう一つ = one more.
v27191c19d7.mnemo: The cow says “**mooo**”: it's **already** time to go back to the barn. もう = **already**.

vb59c87dbf4.frase_furigana: ニャンは 何[なに]を使[つか]う?

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
は: the topic of the sentence

vb59c87dbf4.matiz: Also to spend money or time: お金を使う.

v34c8b33dfc.frase_furigana: 私[わたし]たちは 友達[ともだち]だ。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v34c8b33dfc.matiz: たち makes words for people plural: 子供[こども]たち (children). 僕[ぼく]たち and 俺[おれ]たち are more casual, masculine versions.

v1c5b79d3b1.frase_furigana: 十[じゅう] 時[じ]に 学校[がっこう]に 来[き]ます。
v1c5b79d3b1.frase_es: I come to school at ten.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v1c5b79d3b1.matiz: The base for bigger numbers: 十一 = 11, 二十 = 20. Ten things: 十 (とお).

vff59617945.frase_furigana: ニャンはいつも 眠[ねむ]い。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vff59617945.matiz: Also for habits: “usually”. いつもの = the usual.

ve24ff59cd0.frase_furigana: ニャンはまた 食[た]べる。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
は: the topic of the sentence

ve24ff59cd0.matiz: In goodbyes: また明日 (see you tomorrow), またね (see you).

vab5c95b0e7.frase_furigana: 先生[せんせい]に聞[き]くよ。

gramatica.nota: 聞くよ: plain form + よ to sound sure, instead of 聞きます.
gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence
に: destination, time, where something is

vab5c95b0e7.matiz: The same verb means “to ask”: the person you ask takes に. Listening closely (to music, say) is sometimes written 聴く.

v0ef510d2ad.frase_furigana: いつ 日本[にほん]に 行[い]きますか。
v0ef510d2ad.frase_es: When are you going to Japan?

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v0ef510d2ad.matiz: Usually no に after it. いつも = always; いつか = someday.

ve14162ce54.frase_furigana: 子供[こども]が 三[さん] 人[にん]います。

gramatica.nota: 〜人 counts people: 三人 (さんにん).

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

ve14162ce54.matiz: Also “son or daughter”: 子供[こども]が 二人[ふたり]いる = I have two kids. Often written 子[こ]ども.

va52e26c4b2.frase: ニャンが私の本を取った。
va52e26c4b2.frase_furigana: ニャンが 私[わたし]の 本[ほん]を取[と]った。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

va52e26c4b2.matiz: An all-purpose verb: get a grade ( 点[てん]を 取[と]る), take something off ( 帽子[ぼうし]を 取[と]る), make a reservation ( 予約[よやく]を 取[と]る).

va57d466068.frase: 今日は仕事がありますか。
va57d466068.frase_furigana: 今日[きょう]は仕事[しごと]がありますか。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

va57d466068.matiz: A job or a specific task. お仕事は? = What do you do (for a living)?

v61e79ab71e.frase: 友達が本をくれました。
v61e79ab71e.frase_furigana: 友達[ともだち]が 本[ほん]をくれました。
v61e79ab71e.frase_es: A friend gave me a book.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v61e79ab71e.matiz: Always toward you or your side (family, friends). When you're the one giving, it's あげる. English uses “give” both ways; Japanese splits them.
v61e79ab71e.mnemo: “**Cool**! **Re**ally for **me**?” くれる = someone **gives me** something.

v8c85e3771e.frase: みんなで日本語を勉強します。
v8c85e3771e.frase_furigana: みんなで 日本[にほん] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう]します。

gramatica.nota: みんなで = “all together”.
gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v8c85e3771e.matiz: Formal: みなさん (when talking to a group, like “everyone” in a speech). Also written 皆.

v1938d64f5e.frase_furigana: 本[ほん]をここに置[お]きます。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v1938d64f5e.matiz: To put something somewhere and leave it there. As 〜ておく it means “to do something in advance”.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v40f2568232.matiz: With a past verb: 食べた後 = after eating. 後で = later. Also “what's left”: あと五分 = five more minutes.

v885f80f47b.frase: ニャンはよく食べますね。
v885f80f47b.frase_furigana: ニャンはよく 食[た]べますね。
v885f80f47b.frase_es: Nyan sure eats a lot, doesn't he?

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
は: the topic of the sentence

v885f80f47b.matiz: よく分かりました is a very natural “Got it, perfectly clear”. It also means “often” or “a lot”, as in this sentence: よく行く = I go often.
v885f80f47b.mnemo: よく comes from よい, **good**, just like English **good** → **well**.

va09684d234.frase: ごめんなさい、知りませんでした。
va09684d234.frase_furigana: ごめんなさい、 知[し]りませんでした。
va09684d234.tono: ゴメンナサイ
va09684d234.matiz: For a real apology. すみません also works to get attention or to say thanks. Among friends: ごめん.

vdd352c3305.frase_furigana: 五[ご] 時[じ]に 来[き]ました。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v07ce688900.frase_furigana: おにぎりを作[つく]ります。
v07ce688900.matiz: Making by creating something: food, objects, even friends. Doing an action is する, so “make a mistake” is not 作る.

v77638c7713.frase_furigana: 子供[こども]の時[とき]、 日本[にほん]にいた。
v77638c7713.frase_es: When I was a kid, I lived in Japan.

gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v77638c7713.matiz: After a verb, an adjective, or a noun + の, it means “when”: 子供の時 = when I was a child.

va6a5c7c79a.tono: モンダイ

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
は: the topic of the sentence

va6a5c7c79a.matiz: A problem, and also a question on a test. 問題ない = no problem.

vd245e72ea1.frase: ニャンはおにぎりを出した。
vd245e72ea1.frase_furigana: ニャンはおにぎりを出[だ]した。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vd245e72ea1.matiz: Also to hand in (宿題を出す, hand in homework) or to send (手紙を出す, mail a letter). It's the transitive partner of 出る.

v18d4a1c24d.frase_furigana: 彼女[かのじょ]は 日本[にほん] 語[ご]の 先生[せんせい]です。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v18d4a1c24d.matiz: Also means “girlfriend”. That's partly why people normally use the person's name instead.

vd049a4a229.frase_furigana: 私[わたし]も同[おな]じだよ。

gramatica.nota: だよ: だ + よ, to say something firmly to a friend.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vd049a4a229.matiz: Goes straight before a noun with no な or の: 同じ本 (the same book). It looks like a な-adjective but skips the な.

v0b597be0a6.tono: コンバンハ
v0b597be0a6.matiz: A greeting for when you meet someone in the evening. Like English “good evening”, it's a hello, not a goodbye; at bedtime you say おやすみ.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vf4238a35ef.matiz: The noun form of 話す (to speak). 話をする = to have a chat. It also means “story” or “what someone is talking about”: 何の話? = What are you talking about?

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

vfb18237587.matiz: Near the listener. Far from both of you is あそこ (over there). English “there” covers both.
vfb18237587.mnemo: “**So**, what's **there**?” The こそあど family: **そ** is near you. そこ = **there**, where you are.

v8fc5947d00.frase_furigana: 明日[あした]、考[かんが]える。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v8fc5947d00.matiz: 思う is having an opinion or a feeling; 考える is thinking something through, turning it over in your head.

vdc89d234e4.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]に 名前[なまえ]をつけます。
vdc89d234e4.frase_es: I'll give the cat a name.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vdc89d234e4.matiz: Almost always written in kana. Turning something off is 消[け]す. Many uses, all about attaching something: switching on a light, putting on cream, giving a name (名前をつける).
vdc89d234e4.mnemo: Its kanji 点ける has a **dot** (点): picture the red dot on a switch. Press it, “**tsk**!”, and the light comes **on**: つける.

v96f16f484d.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]が 家[いえ]に入[はい]ります。
v96f16f484d.frase_es: The cat goes into the house.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
に: destination, time, where something is

v96f16f484d.matiz: A う-verb even though it ends in いる: 入ります, 入らない. お風呂に入る = to take a bath (literally, “get into the bath”). Also to join a club.

v016d147257.frase_furigana: 今[いま]、お 金[かね]がない。
v016d147257.frase_es: I don't have any money right now.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v016d147257.matiz: The normal, polite form; plain 金 sounds rough. お金持ち = a rich person.

vdca867ed43.frase_furigana: 今日[きょう]はいい日[ひ]だね。
vdca867ed43.frase_es: It's a lovely day today, isn't it?

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vdca867ed43.matiz: ひ is a particular day and also the sun: 日[ひ]が 昇[のぼ]る (the sun rises). In dates and counting it changes reading: 一日[いちにち], 三日[みっか].

v8d07ff2178.frase_furigana: 新[あたら]しい 本[ほん]を買[か]います。
v8d07ff2178.frase_es: I'm going to buy a new book.
v8d07ff2178.matiz: A う-verb: 買います, 買わない (the う turns into わ).

v800ecd9277.frase_es: I have a cat at home.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

v800ecd9277.matiz: 家 is the house as a building; うち is home, “my place”, the family. It also means “our”: うちの猫 = our cat.
v800ecd9277.mnemo: “**Ooh**, **chee**se and a warm fire!” うち = **home**, sweet home.

v7b034bdcb7.frase_furigana: ニャンの目[め]、 大[おお]きいね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v7b034bdcb7.matiz: Also “eyesight”: 目がいい = to have good eyes. After a number it makes ordinals: 二つ目 = the second one.

gramatica.nota: 〜てください = “please do…”. 気をつける = to be careful.
gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

vc81b862c53.matiz: Hard to translate on its own, but it shows up in tons of expressions: 気をつける (be careful), 気持ち (feeling), 気になる (to be on your mind). Learn it inside phrases.

v3a77da4531.matiz: まだ + a negative ている form = not yet: まだ食べていない = I haven't eaten yet. The opposite is もう.
v3a77da4531.mnemo: “**Mada**m, the soup is **still** not ready!” まだ = **still / not yet**.

v59619beceb.frase_furigana: 一[いち]から 十[じゅう]まで 書[か]きます。
v59619beceb.frase_es: I'll write from one to ten.

gramatica.nota: から… まで = “from… to”.

v59619beceb.matiz: 一から = from scratch. With native Japanese counters it changes: 一つ (ひとつ), 一人 (ひとり).

v6be369515a.frase_furigana: ニャンが 水[みず]をかけた。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v6be369515a.matiz: A verb with lots of uses: pouring or splashing over something, hanging, putting on glasses, sitting down. 電話をかける = to make a phone call.

vffa102eaa8.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん]は 猫[ねこ]が多[おお]いね。
vffa102eaa8.frase_es: There sure are a lot of cats in Japan.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

vffa102eaa8.matiz: Unlike English “many”, it doesn't usually go right before a noun: “many people” is 多[おお]くの 人[ひと] or たくさんの 人[ひと], not 多[おお]い 人[ひと]. It's happiest at the end: 猫が多い = there are lots of cats.

vbb2f8b6227.frase: ニャンにおにぎりをあげる。
vbb2f8b6227.frase_furigana: ニャンにおにぎりをあげる。

gramatica.nota: に marks who you give something to.
gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is
Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

vbb2f8b6227.matiz: From you (or your side) to others. When someone gives something to you, it's くれる. Same origin as 上げる, “to raise”.
vbb2f8b6227.mnemo: You lift the gift **up** and hand it **over**: あげる (related to 上げる, to raise) = to **give** to someone else.

v32758892c8.frase: 日本語が少しわかります。
v32758892c8.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]が少[すこ]しわかります。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v32758892c8.matiz: More formal than ちょっと. 少しずつ = little by little.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

vedb6dfb30e.matiz: Also “help, labor”, just like English “a hand”: 手が足りない = we're short of hands.

vbefce21fe6.frase: ニャンと日本語で話す。
vbefce21fe6.frase_furigana: ニャンと 日本[にほん] 語[ご]で話[はな]す。
vbefce21fe6.frase_es: I talk with Nyan in Japanese.

gramatica.nota: で also marks the language or means: 日本語で = “in Japanese”.
gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
と and や: lists of things

vbefce21fe6.matiz: To speak, talk, tell. 言う is “to say” something specific. Speaking a language: 日本語を話す.

v309af5c529.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]は 本[ほん]の上[うえ]にいます。
v309af5c529.frase_es: The cat is on top of the book.

gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v309af5c529.matiz: Position: 机の上 = on the desk. Also “higher, older”: 年上 = older (in age).

gramatica.nota: 来た: plain past. Among friends, 来た instead of 来ました.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v6ac8c6f7bb.matiz: 一人で = alone, on my own. 一人っ子 = an only child.

v708880825d.frase_furigana: 学校[がっこう]に車[くるま]で 行[い]く。
v708880825d.frase_es: I go to school by car.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
で: where an action happens / with what
に: destination, time, where something is

v708880825d.matiz: 車椅子 = wheelchair. In 電車 (train) the same kanji is read しゃ.

v38c025450d.tono: オヤスミ
v38c025450d.matiz: Said when going to bed (or when the other person is). More polite: おやすみなさい.

v58524b90c3.matiz: Masculine and soft: used by boys, and by men in relaxed settings. Less rough than 俺. English has one “I”; Japanese picks one to fit who you are and who you're talking to.

vcde18639a4.frase: このおにぎりはとてもおいしいです。
vcde18639a4.frase_furigana: このおにぎりはとてもおいしいです。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vcde18639a4.matiz: With a negative it means “no way”: とても無理 = completely impossible. In conversation people often say すごく instead.
vcde18639a4.mnemo: とても ≈ “**to the mo**(on)”: I love it **very** much, all the way **to the moon**!

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

ve9384cc575.matiz: Among friends, 悪い works as an apology, like “my bad”. 気分が悪い = to feel sick.

vc1357f4d72.frase: ニャン、水を入れてください。
vc1357f4d72.frase_furigana: ニャン、 水[みず]を入[い]れてください。
vc1357f4d72.frase_es: Nyan, please pour some water in.

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

vc1357f4d72.matiz: Also used for making drinks: お 茶[ちゃ]を 入[い]れる = to make tea.

ve4df70ccca.frase: 日本語の言葉を書きます。
ve4df70ccca.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]の言葉[ことば]を 書[か]きます。
ve4df70ccca.matiz: A single word, and also “language, way of speaking”. 単語 is “word” as a vocabulary item.

v599b2deea2.frase_furigana: 一[いち]万[まん] 人[にん]が 来[き]ました。

gramatica.nota: 一万 = 10,000: Japanese counts in blocks of ten thousand.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v599b2deea2.matiz: Japan counts in blocks of 万, not thousands: 10万 = a hundred thousand, 100万 = a million. 万一 = just in case.

v821f2c5324.frase_es: Oh no, that's not true at all.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v821f2c5324.matiz: こんな (like this), そんな (like that), あんな (like that, over there). そんなことない is the standard modest reply to a compliment: “Oh, not at all.”

vd88fd1a97c.frase_furigana: その男[おとこ]、 誰[だれ]?
vd88fd1a97c.matiz: Plain 男 can sound rough, a bit like “that guy”; the neutral phrase is 男の人. Formal: 男性.

vc4fbc65d8c.frase: ニャンはあまり勉強しません。
vc4fbc65d8c.frase_furigana: ニャンはあまり 勉強[べんきょう]しません。

gramatica.nota: あまり goes with a negative verb: “not much”.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vc4fbc65d8c.matiz: With a negative it means “not much, not very”. In the positive (あまりに) it means “too, excessively”. Casual: あんまり.
vc4fbc65d8c.mnemo: “**Ah, Mari** doesn't eat **much**.” あまり always comes with a negative: **not much**.

vf1d5fc9009.frase_furigana: 先生[せんせい]に 本[ほん]をもらった。
vf1d5fc9009.frase_es: I got a book from my teacher.

gramatica.nota: 〜にもらう: に marks who you receive something from.
gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vf1d5fc9009.matiz: The giver can take から or に: 彼女から/に もらう. English often says “X gave me”, where Japanese prefers “I received from X”.
vf1d5fc9009.mnemo: “**Mor**e? **Ah**, **oo**h, thank you!” you say as you **receive** gift after gift: もらう.

v2a5ba4088f.frase_furigana: お 金[かね]が必要[ひつよう]だ。
v2a5ba4088f.tono: ヒツヨウ

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v2a5ba4088f.matiz: “I need X” is Xが必要です: English uses a verb, Japanese says “X is necessary”. The opposite is 不要 (unnecessary).

v78aa9dced0.matiz: Like 少し, but more conversational; it also means “a moment”: ちょっと待って = wait a sec. A trailing ちょっと… is a soft “no”: “well, that's a bit…”.
v78aa9dced0.mnemo: ちょっと sounds like “**a shot**”: just **a bit**, a tiny amount.

vc596eb8a7f.frase_furigana: 六[ろく] 時[じ]に 家[いえ]に 来[き]てください。
vc596eb8a7f.frase_es: Please come to my place at six.

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

vc596eb8a7f.matiz: Six things: 六つ (むっつ). With some counters it shortens: 六本 = ろっぽん.

v9232ae5e06.frase: ニャンがお金をしまった。
v9232ae5e06.frase_furigana: ニャンがお 金[かね]をしまった。

gramatica.nota: しまった: plain past of しまう, very natural among friends.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v9232ae5e06.matiz: It's also a helper verb (〜てしまう, “to end up doing”), which comes in a later lesson. On its own, しまった! means “Oh no!”.

v33a1e26558.frase_furigana: 友達[ともだち]に電話[でんわ]をかける。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
に: destination, time, where something is

v33a1e26558.matiz: 電話する = to call. A cellphone is 携帯 or スマホ. When you pick up, you say もしもし.

vaf7c5224c1.frase: 漢字は時間がかかります。
vaf7c5224c1.frase_furigana: 漢字[かんじ]は 時間[じかん]がかかります。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
は: the topic of the sentence

vaf7c5224c1.matiz: For time and money: 時間[じかん]がかかる (to take time), お 金[かね]がかかる (to cost money). In this sense it's written in kana.
vaf7c5224c1.mnemo: The taxi meter goes “**ka-ka-ka**” as you ride: how long it **takes** and how much it **costs**.

vd595b6806b.frase_furigana: 明日[あした]、 友達[ともだち]に会[あ]う。

gramatica.nota: The person you meet takes に: 友達に会う.
gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is
Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

vd595b6806b.matiz: With と it's meeting by mutual arrangement; with に, going to see someone or running into them. English “see” also means meet, but seeing a movie is 見る.

vc8d4497961.frase_furigana: さようなら、 先生[せんせい]。
vc8d4497961.tono: サヨウナラ
vc8d4497961.matiz: Sounds like a long or final goodbye. Kids say it to their teachers, but among friends people say じゃあね or またね.

vd52f01a905.frase: どうして日本語を勉強しますか。
vd52f01a905.frase_furigana: どうして 日本[にほん] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう]しますか。
vd52f01a905.tono: ドウシテ
vd52f01a905.matiz: The most neutral one. なぜ is more formal; なんで is more casual.

vfef1257d79.frase_furigana: どんな 本[ほん]が 好[す]き?
vfef1257d79.frase_es: What kind of books do you like?

gramatica.titulo: Liking and being good at: が with adjectives
が: who or what (the identified subject)

vfef1257d79.matiz: Always before a noun: どんな人 (what kind of person). こんな, そんな, あんな = “this / that kind of…”.
vfef1257d79.mnemo: The こそあど family: **ど** asks. どんな + noun = **what kind of…?**

v96cb7d6225.frase_furigana: 学校[がっこう]の方[ほう]に 行[い]きます。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v96cb7d6225.matiz: Used a lot for comparing: こっちの方がいい = this one is better. Same kanji as かた (person, polite).

v26e2ad06d8.frase_furigana: こんな 本[ほん]が 好[す]きだよ。

gramatica.titulo: Liking and being good at: が with adjectives
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vb38ff7ac28.frase: 先生が日本語を教えます。
vb38ff7ac28.frase_furigana: 先生[せんせい]が 日本[にほん] 語[ご]を教[おし]えます。
vb38ff7ac28.tono: オシエル

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

vb38ff7ac28.matiz: Not just in class: also “to tell, let someone know” a piece of information. 道を教えて = Can you tell me the way? English says “tell”, Japanese says “teach”.

va8473139b9.frase_furigana: 五[ご] 時[じ]に 家[いえ]に帰[かえ]る。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
に: destination, time, where something is

va8473139b9.matiz: Going back to where you belong: home, your own country. Careful: it's a う-verb even though it ends in える: 帰ります, 帰らない.

vccff0e66b2.frase_furigana: 次[つぎ]は 何[なん]ですか。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v1f1db35c9b.frase_furigana: 八[はち] 時[じ]に 学校[がっこう]に 行[い]きます。
v1f1db35c9b.frase_es: I go to school at eight.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v1f1db35c9b.matiz: Shortens before some counters: 八個 (はっこ), 八本 (はっぽん). Eight things: 八つ (やっつ).

v18afb8ceef.frase_furigana: 明日[あした]、会社[かいしゃ]に 行[い]きます。
v18afb8ceef.frase_es: I'm going to the office tomorrow.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v5ae9f1be29.frase_furigana: 二人[ふたり]で 行[い]きましょう。
v5ae9f1be29.frase_es: Let's go, just the two of us.

gramatica.nota: 〜ましょう = “let's…”, for suggesting something.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v7b70c76bb9.frase_furigana: それ、ちょっと違[ちが]うよ。
v7b70c76bb9.frase_es: That's not quite right, you know.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v7b70c76bb9.matiz: 違います = No, that's not it (softer than いいえ). It's a verb, not an adjective: 違った, 違わない. Japanese uses the same word for “different” and “wrong”.

vcb703e2149.frase_furigana: しかし、ニャンは 眠[ねむ]いです。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vcb703e2149.matiz: More for writing than でも, much like “however” vs. “but”.

vaf51de5f4d.frase_furigana: ニャン、 何[なに]持[も]ってる?
vaf51de5f4d.frase_es: Nyan, what have you got there?

gramatica.nota: 持っている = to have, to be carrying (a lasting state). In speech: 持ってる.
gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

vaf51de5f4d.matiz: To hold, carry or own. Not for people: “I have a brother” is 兄がいる. English “have” is much broader.

v8f976aa396.frase_furigana: 一緒[いっしょ]に 食[た]べましょう。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v8f976aa396.matiz: 一緒に = together. 一緒に行こう = Let's go together. Also “the same”: 私と一緒 = same as me.

vd0d563daf9.frase: おにぎりを一つください。
vd0d563daf9.frase_furigana: おにぎりを一[ひと]つください。
vd0d563daf9.matiz: For counting things: 一つ, 二つ, 三つ… This native series works for most objects when you don't know the right counter.

v8babbd762d.frase: ニャンはおにぎりが一番好きだ。
v8babbd762d.frase_furigana: ニャンはおにぎりが一番[いちばん] 好[す]きだ。
v8babbd762d.tono: イチバン
v8babbd762d.frase_es: Nyan likes onigiri more than anything.

gramatica.titulo: Liking and being good at: が with adjectives
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v8babbd762d.matiz: Before an adjective it makes the superlative: 一番大きい = the biggest. On its own it means “number one, first”.

v59bbbb5ae5.frase: 日本語を勉強します。そして、漢字も書きます。
v59bbbb5ae5.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう]します。そして、 漢字[かんじ]も 書[か]きます。
v59bbbb5ae5.frase_es: I study Japanese. And I write kanji, too.
v59bbbb5ae5.matiz: Links sentences: “and”, “and then”. It doesn't join nouns; for “cats and dogs” use と.
v59bbbb5ae5.mnemo: そ (that) + して (doing): “having done that”… **and then**.

v65d8fe1c1e.frase_furigana: 長[なが]い 話[はなし]ですね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v65d8fe1c1e.matiz: For space and time: 長[なが]い 夏休[なつやす]み (a long summer vacation). The opposite is 短[みじか]い.

vcda8dce3e7.frase_furigana: ニャンの顔[かお]、 大[おお]きいね。
vcda8dce3e7.frase_es: Nyan's got a big face, huh?

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vcda8dce3e7.matiz: Also an expression: 嬉しそうな顔 = a happy face. 顔を出す = to show your face, drop by.

v983fc484ed.frase: ニャンはたくさん食べました。
v983fc484ed.frase_furigana: ニャンはたくさん 食[た]べました。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v983fc484ed.matiz: Almost always in kana. No particle before a verb: たくさん食べる. Before a noun it takes の: たくさんの猫.
v983fc484ed.mnemo: “**Tuck** in, **son**, there's **a lot**!” たくさん = **lots, plenty**.

v6218a49eae.frase_furigana: 新[あたら]しい 本[ほん]が欲[ほ]しいよ。
v6218a49eae.frase_es: I really want a new book.

gramatica.nota: What you want to have takes が: 本が欲しい.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v6218a49eae.matiz: For wanting things. Wanting to do something is 〜たい. What someone else wants is said with 欲[ほ]しがる, because Japanese avoids stating other people's feelings directly.

v3224ea4ae5.frase_furigana: どの 本[ほん]がいいですか。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v3224ea4ae5.matiz: For choosing among several of the same kind: どの本 = which book? Always followed by a noun.
v3224ea4ae5.mnemo: The こそあど family: **ど** asks. どの + noun: どの本 = **which** book?

v693e343df4.frase: ちょっと待ってください。
v693e343df4.frase_furigana: ちょっと待[ま]ってください。

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

v693e343df4.matiz: 待って! = Wait! What you wait for takes を, with no “for”: 友達を待つ = to wait for a friend. Looking forward to something is 楽しみにする.

vc2500e2218.frase_furigana: あそこに 猫[ねこ]がいます。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

vc2500e2218.matiz: Watch the shape: unlike ここ and そこ, it has an extra そ. It's あそこ, not “あこ”.
vc2500e2218.mnemo: “**Ah**, **so** far, **over there**!” The こそあど family: **あ** is away from both of us. あそこ = **over there**.

vf085bd3e3a.frase_furigana: 車[くるま]に乗[の]ります。

gramatica.nota: 乗る takes に: 車に乗る = “to get in the car”.
gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vf085bd3e3a.matiz: Getting off is 降[お]りる, with を: 電車[でんしゃ]を 降[お]りる. English says “take the train”; Japanese says “ride on it”: 電車に乗る.

v3c6960b9da.frase_furigana: でも、ニャンは 眠[ねむ]い。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v3c6960b9da.matiz: Goes at the start of the sentence. It's the normal “but” in conversation.

ve3847590b8.frase: ニャンは「いただきます」って言った。
ve3847590b8.frase_furigana: ニャンは「いただきます」って 言[い]った。
ve3847590b8.tono: イタダキマス

gramatica.nota: って: the spoken form of と, very natural in conversation.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

ve3847590b8.matiz: Said before eating, to give thanks for the food. English has no real equivalent; it's closer to a tiny grace than to “bon appétit”. It literally means “I humbly receive”. After the meal: ごちそうさま.

v61b5f184a7.frase: この言葉の意味は何ですか。
v61b5f184a7.frase_furigana: この 言葉[ことば]の意味[いみ]は 何[なん]ですか。
v61b5f184a7.matiz: 意味がない = it's pointless. どういう意味? = What do you mean?

vd9fb62e684.frase: ここから学校が見える。
vd9fb62e684.frase_furigana: ここから 学校[がっこう]が見[み]える。
vd9fb62e684.frase_es: You can see the school from here.

gramatica.nota: から = “from”.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
が: who or what (the identified subject)

vd9fb62e684.matiz: Something comes into view by itself, with no effort. English says “I can see…”; Japanese says “…is visible”. Also “to look, seem”: 若く見える = looks young.

va190b4cc9b.frase_furigana: 母[はは]は 先生[せんせい]です。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

va190b4cc9b.matiz: For talking about your own mother. Someone else's mother, or your own when you speak to her: お母さん. A bit like “my mother” vs. “Mom”, but stricter.

vff57823736.frase: ニャンは強くないです。
vff57823736.frase_furigana: ニャンは強[つよ]くないです。

gramatica.nota: Negative of an い-adjective: 強い → 強くない.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vff57823736.matiz: The opposite is 弱い. Also “good at”: 数学に強い = good at math. Strong wind or rain is 強い too.

v099f2c3e63.frase_furigana: ニャンは 食[た]べすぎた。

gramatica.nota: 〜すぎる after a verb stem (食べ + すぎる) = “too much”.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v099f2c3e63.matiz: After another verb: 食べすぎる = to eat too much. After an adjective stem too: 高すぎる = too expensive.

v10c56ae24d.frase: ニャンは部屋でおにぎりを食べすぎた。
v10c56ae24d.frase_furigana: ニャンは部屋[へや]でおにぎりを 食[た]べすぎた。
v10c56ae24d.frase_es: Nyan ate way too many onigiri in his room.

gramatica.nota: 食べすぎた: 〜すぎる again, “ate too much”.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v10c56ae24d.matiz: Both a room and a small rented apartment.
v10c56ae24d.mnemo: “**Hey**, **ya**! Get out of my **room**!” へや = **room**. A special reading.

v69af0d3670.frase: 誰かが日本語を勉強し始めた。
v69af0d3670.frase_furigana: 誰[だれ]かが 日本[にほん] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう]し 始[はじ]めた。

gramatica.nota: 〜始める after a verb stem (勉強し + 始める) = “to start doing”.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v69af0d3670.matiz: 誰 + か = someone: the か works like “some-” in English. 誰も + a negative = nobody.

v4a7772053a.frase: ニャンは百まで書き続けた。
v4a7772053a.frase_furigana: ニャンは百[ひゃく]まで 書[か]き 続[つづ]けた。
v4a7772053a.frase_es: Nyan kept writing all the way to a hundred.

gramatica.nota: 〜続ける = “to keep doing”: 書き続ける.
来なかった: plain negative past (来る → 来ない → 来なかった).

va9425143ae.matiz: More formal than どうして; common in writing and in serious questions.
va9425143ae.mnemo: なぜ sounds a bit like **nosy**: a **nosy** kid keeps asking **why?**

v8fc66af247.frase: 友達がニャンを呼んだ。そして、ニャンが話し出した。
v8fc66af247.frase_furigana: 友達[ともだち]がニャンを呼[よ]んだ。そして、ニャンが 話[はな]し 出[だ]した。
v8fc66af247.frase_es: A friend called Nyan. Then Nyan started talking.

gramatica.nota: 〜出す after a verb stem = to suddenly start doing something: 話し出す.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v8fc66af247.matiz: To call someone over, or to call something by a name. Calling on the phone is 電話する. Also “to invite”: 友達を家に呼ぶ.

v8c151612a3.frase: 食べ終わって、「ごちそうさま」と言った。
v8c151612a3.frase_furigana: 食[た]べ 終[お]わって、「ごちそうさま」と 言[い]った。
v8c151612a3.tono: ゴチソウサマ

gramatica.nota: 〜終わる = “to finish doing”: 食べ終わる.

v8c151612a3.matiz: Said when you finish eating, to the cook or host, or just to the food. More polite: ごちそうさまでした. It pairs with いただきます before the meal.

v6c771d3d4b.frase_furigana: 九[く] 時[じ]に 会社[かいしゃ]に 行[い]きます。
v6c771d3d4b.frase_es: I go to the office at nine.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v6c771d3d4b.matiz: Nine things: 九つ (ここのつ).
v6c771d3d4b.mnemo: People avoid く because it sounds like 苦 (**suffering**), so nine is usually **きゅう**, like a **cue**. Exception: 九時 = くじ.

vc7ccad3248.frase_furigana: 父[ちち]は 日本[にほん]にいる。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

vc7ccad3248.matiz: For talking about your own father. Someone else's father, or your own when you speak to him: お父さん.

v3bc51f4287.frase_furigana: 大[おお]きな 家[いえ]ですね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v3bc51f4287.matiz: Only goes before a noun: 大きな家. To say “it's big”, use 大きい. It isn't a な-adjective: there's no “大きだ”.

vcffd5f6deb.frase: 学校は三時に終わります。
vcffd5f6deb.frase_furigana: 学校[がっこう]は 三[さん] 時[じ]に終[お]わります。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vcffd5f6deb.matiz: Something ends. To finish something yourself: 終える (formal) or 終わらせる.

gramatica.nota: 〜たい = “I want to (do)”: 食べる → 食べたい.

vc4842fd138.matiz: Always comparative: “more than now”. It isn't used for “more” in sums or counts.
vc4842fd138.mnemo: もっと even sounds like **more**. Rev the **mo**torbike: “**More**! **More**!”

vbf1af1a1ea.frase_furigana: 学校[がっこう]まで歩[ある]きます。

gramatica.nota: まで = “as far as, to”.

vbf1af1a1ea.matiz: A う-verb. 歩いて行く = to go on foot.

v8db2ef306d.frase: 大きい声で話してください。
v8db2ef306d.frase_furigana: 大[おお]きい声[こえ]で 話[はな]してください。

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください
で: where an action happens / with what

v8db2ef306d.matiz: The voice of people and animals, and birdsong. Sounds made by things are 音. English can say “sound” for both; Japanese keeps them apart: a meow is a 声, a slammed door is an 音.

v6370f6076d.frase_furigana: あの 人[ひと]、 誰[だれ]?
v6370f6076d.matiz: On its own, あの… is a filler, like “um…, excuse me…”, to start talking.
v6370f6076d.mnemo: The こそあど family: **あ** is far from both of us. あの + noun: あの本 = **that** book over there.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v39a1913d9a.matiz: Also brains: 頭がいい = smart (literally “good head”). 頭が痛い = I have a headache.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v9621133adc.matiz: Usually has something in front: いい子 (good kid), 男の子 (boy), 女の子 (girl). いい子 is also what you say to a good pet.

v8bbfa06839.frase_furigana: 電話[でんわ]を切[き]ります。
v8bbfa06839.frase_es: I'm going to hang up now.
v8bbfa06839.matiz: Also to hang up the phone ( 電話[でんわ]を 切[き]る) and to switch off (スイッチを 切[き]る). 着[き]る (to wear) sounds the same, but 切る is a う-verb: 切った vs. 着た.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v30547e7d94.matiz: For two options; for three or more, use どれ. The polite form of どっち. Also a polite “where”: どちらへ? = Where are you headed?
v30547e7d94.mnemo: ど asks, ちら means side: “which side?”. At a fork in the road you pick one: どちら = **which of the two**.

vf225a115fc.frase_furigana: どこの国[くに]の 人[ひと]ですか。
vf225a115fc.matiz: Also “homeland, home region”: お国はどちらですか = Where are you from? (polite)

v989396ad6b.frase: 今日は学校がない。だから、ニャンは家にいる。
v989396ad6b.frase_furigana: 今日[きょう]は 学校[がっこう]がない。だから、ニャンは 家[いえ]にいる。
v989396ad6b.frase_es: There's no school today. So Nyan is at home.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
が: who or what (the identified subject)

ve5a5f38233.frase: これ、ニャンの写真だよ。
ve5a5f38233.frase_furigana: これ、ニャンの写真[しゃしん]だよ。
ve5a5f38233.frase_es: Look, this is a photo of Nyan.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

ve5a5f38233.matiz: 写真を撮る = to take a picture (with 撮る, not する).

v0489673a47.frase: 家と学校の間に猫がいます。
v0489673a47.frase_furigana: 家[いえ]と 学校[がっこう]の間[あいだ]に 猫[ねこ]がいます。
v0489673a47.frase_es: There's a cat between the house and the school.

gramatica.titulo: と and や: lists of things
が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

v0489673a47.matiz: あいだ is the gap between two things, in space or in time: 夏休[なつやす]みの 間[あいだ] = during summer vacation.

vb21caaff91.frase: 学校に千人の子供がいます。
vb21caaff91.frase_furigana: 学校[がっこう]に千[せん] 人[にん]の 子供[こども]がいます。
vb21caaff91.frase_es: There are a thousand children at the school.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

vba0a60a702.frase: ニャンはテレビを見てる。
vba0a60a702.frase_furigana: ニャンはテレビを 見[み]てる。

gramatica.nota: 見てる = the spoken form of 見ている.
gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
は: the topic of the sentence

vba0a60a702.matiz: テレビを見る = to watch TV. テレビ番組 = a TV show.
vba0a60a702.mnemo: English **tele**vision, cut short Japanese-style: **tere**-**bi**, just like saying “telly”.

v37f43ddee7.frase_furigana: 名前[なまえ]を忘[わす]れた。
v37f43ddee7.tono: ワスレル
v37f43ddee7.matiz: Also “to leave something behind”: 傘を忘れた = I left my umbrella behind.

v8b5162f2e6.frase: 日本語の本が少ないね。
v8b5162f2e6.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]の 本[ほん]が少[すく]ないね。
v8b5162f2e6.frase_es: There aren't many books in Japanese, are there?

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v8b5162f2e6.matiz: The opposite of 多[おお]い. Careful: 少[すこ]し is “a little”; 少[すく]ない is “few, scarce”. Same kanji, different reading.

vd5d968be04.frase: 日本語の勉強を始めた。
vd5d968be04.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]の 勉強[べんきょう]を始[はじ]めた。
vd5d968be04.tono: ハジメル
vd5d968be04.matiz: Someone starts something: 勉強を始める. When something starts by itself, it's 始まる: 学校が始まる.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v671c6a9df0.matiz: 先に = first, ahead of others: 先に行って = go on ahead. Also the tip or end of something: 指の先 = fingertip.

v22cd885bef.frase_furigana: それは体[からだ]に 悪[わる]いです。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v22cd885bef.matiz: Also health: 体に悪い = bad for you. 体に気をつけて = take care of yourself.

vbb4ec07da0.frase_furigana: 父[ちち]は 会社[かいしゃ]で働[はたら]いてる。
vbb4ec07da0.tono: ハタラク
vbb4ec07da0.frase_es: My dad works for a company.

gramatica.nota: 〜ている also tells what someone does for a living. In speech: 働いてる.
gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
で: where an action happens / with what
は: the topic of the sentence

vbb4ec07da0.matiz: 働く is the activity; 仕事 is work as a noun. Also “to function”: 頭が働かない = my brain isn't working.

v0b1c31897a.frase_furigana: どうぞ、 食[た]べてください。

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

v0b1c31897a.matiz: For offering something or letting someone go first. When you're the one asking for something, use お 願[ねが]いします or ください. English “please” covers both; Japanese splits them.
v0b1c31897a.mnemo: Holding the door open: “**Do**… **so**, **go ahead**!” どうぞ = **after you / here you are**.

v837f3d7d40.frase: ニャンは三時間以上、テレビを見ながら食べた。
v837f3d7d40.frase_furigana: ニャンは 三[さん] 時間[じかん]以上[いじょう]、テレビを 見[み]ながら 食[た]べた。
v837f3d7d40.frase_es: Nyan ate for over three hours while watching TV.

gramatica.nota: 〜ながら = doing two things at once; the main action is the second one (見ながら食べた).

v837f3d7d40.matiz: It includes the number itself: 30度以上 = 30 degrees or more (English “over 30” usually doesn't). At the end of a talk, 以上です = that's all.

v76b3c8dcf9.frase: 先生はいい人だし、本をいただいた。
v76b3c8dcf9.frase_furigana: 先生[せんせい]はいい 人[ひと]だし、 本[ほん]をいただいた。
v76b3c8dcf9.tono: イタダク
v76b3c8dcf9.frase_es: My teacher is so kind, and even gave me a book.

gramatica.nota: 〜し lists reasons or facts: Xだし、Yし.

v76b3c8dcf9.matiz: Also the humble way to say eat or drink: that's where いただきます comes from. As a helper verb (〜ていただく) it's written in kana.

v5e8d572fb2.frase: 夜はテレビを見ながら勉強する。
v5e8d572fb2.frase_furigana: 夜[よる]はテレビを 見[み]ながら 勉強[べんきょう]する。
v5e8d572fb2.frase_es: At night I study while watching TV.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v5e8d572fb2.matiz: From nightfall on. Late afternoon to early evening is 夕方; daytime is 昼. English “evening” overlaps both 夕方 and 夜.

v05f1d2a5b4.frase: 昨日は時間もあったし、勉強した。
v05f1d2a5b4.frase_furigana: 昨日[きのう]は 時間[じかん]もあったし、 勉強[べんきょう]した。
v05f1d2a5b4.frase_es: I had time yesterday, so I studied.

gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

v05f1d2a5b4.matiz: No に after it. Formal: さくじつ.
v05f1d2a5b4.mnemo: “**Key? No**, I lost it **yesterday**!” きのう = **yesterday**. A special reading that doesn't come from its kanji.

vf25493720d.frase: 彼は大学で働きながら勉強している。
vf25493720d.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]は大学[だいがく]で 働[はたら]きながら 勉強[べんきょう]している。
vf25493720d.tono: ダイガク
vf25493720d.frase_es: He's studying at university while working.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

v26a5a53055.matiz: Getting up from a chair, or being on your feet. Getting up out of bed is 起きる; English “get up” covers both.

vaf09e8bc28.frase_furigana: こちらは 私[わたし]の 先生[せんせい]です。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vaf09e8bc28.matiz: A polite version of ここ, これ and even “this person”: こちらは田中さんです (This is Ms. Tanaka). It's the polite way to introduce someone.
vaf09e8bc28.mnemo: The こそあど family: **こ** is close to me. こちら = **this way**, said politely.

v17b479dfc7.frase: 日本の生活はどうですか。
v17b479dfc7.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん]の生活[せいかつ]はどうですか。
v17b479dfc7.tono: セイカツ
v17b479dfc7.matiz: Everyday life: home, work, routine. Someone's whole life is 人生; life as being alive is 命. English uses “life” for all three.

gramatica.nota: To say where you live, use 住んでいる. In speech: 住んでる?
gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
に: destination, time, where something is

v8046652e3f.matiz: Living in a place. Being alive, living your life, is 生きる. It almost always appears as 住んでいる, even where English uses the simple “I live”.

v1675e2b413.frase_furigana: いろいろな 本[ほん]を 読[よ]む。
v1675e2b413.tono: イロイロ
v1675e2b413.frase_es: I read all kinds of books.

gramatica.nota: いろいろ takes な before a noun.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v1675e2b413.matiz: Also an adverb: 色々[いろいろ]ありがとう = thanks for everything. Very often written in kana.

vd33435fccb.frase: この店はおいしいです。
vd33435fccb.frase_furigana: この店[みせ]はおいしいです。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vd33435fccb.matiz: Any business with premises: shop, bar, restaurant. 〜 屋[や] = …shop: 本屋[ほんや] (bookstore).

vb909b7716b.frase_furigana: こう 書[か]いてください。

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

vb909b7716b.matiz: The way the speaker is showing. そう is the way the other person said; ああ, a way over there.
vb909b7716b.mnemo: The こそあど family: **こ** is close to me. こう = **like this**, the way I'm doing it.

v0ffd611510.frase_furigana: 今日[きょう]は早[はや]いね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
は: the topic of the sentence

v0ffd611510.matiz: Early, soon. Fast speed is written 速い, with the same reading. English “early” and “fast” are different words; in Japanese they sound the same and only the kanji tells them apart.

v4c3978d3a7.frase: 彼はアメリカの人です。
v4c3978d3a7.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]はアメリカの 人[ひと]です。
v4c3978d3a7.tono: アメリカ

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v4637f4f2db.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん]は初[はじ]めてです。
v4637f4f2db.frase_es: It's my first time in Japan.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v4637f4f2db.matiz: Don't mix it up with 始[はじ]めて (the て-form of 始[はじ]める, to start): they sound the same. And 最初[さいしょ] is “the beginning”, not “for the first time”.

vce193894db.frase: この単語の意味がわからない。
vce193894db.frase_furigana: この単語[たんご]の 意味[いみ]がわからない。
vce193894db.frase_es: I don't understand what this word means.

gramatica.nota: わからない: plain negative (わかる → わからない), used among friends instead of わかりません.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

vce193894db.matiz: 言葉 is “word, language” in general; 単語 is each individual word, the kind on flashcards.

v391ba0a006.frase_furigana: 家族[かぞく]は 何人[なんにん]ですか。
v391ba0a006.frase_es: How many people are in your family?

gramatica.nota: 何人 (なんにん) = “how many people”.

v391ba0a006.matiz: Your own family. Someone else's, said respectfully: ご家族.

vd69cc289f5.matiz: With a positive it means “almost all”: ほとんどの 人[ひと] (most people). With a negative, “hardly any”: ほとんどない.
vd69cc289f5.mnemo: Ho-**TON**-do: a **ton** of stuff makes the truck **almost** full.

v792651d59c.frase: 先生の電話を受けました。
v792651d59c.frase_furigana: 先生[せんせい]の 電話[でんわ]を受[う]けました。
v792651d59c.frase_es: I got a call from my teacher.
v792651d59c.matiz: Receiving something that comes at you: a blow, a call, damage. 試験を受ける = to take an exam (English says “take”, Japanese says “receive”).

v2a750e33d5.frase: その場合は、電話してください。
v2a750e33d5.frase_furigana: その場合[ばあい]は、 電話[でんわ]してください。
v2a750e33d5.frase_es: In that case, please call me.

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください
は: the topic of the sentence

v2a750e33d5.matiz: 〜 場合[ばあい]は = in case…, if…; more formal than 〜たら, typical of instructions and notices.

v73887932ef.frase_furigana: きれいな 部屋[へや]だね。

gramatica.nota: きれい looks like an い-adjective, but it's a な-adjective: きれいな部屋.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v73887932ef.matiz: Pretty and clean at once: 綺麗な部屋 can mean either. Almost always written in kana: きれい.

v51d0ab4ad9.tono: オカアサン
v51d0ab4ad9.matiz: For calling your own mother, or for talking about someone else's.
v51d0ab4ad9.mnemo: Special reading: 母 here is **かあ**, not はは. Mom caws like a crow: “**Kaa**! Come home!”

v748ae7003f.frase: その女の人は誰ですか。
v748ae7003f.frase_furigana: その女[おんな]の 人[ひと]は 誰[だれ]ですか。
v748ae7003f.matiz: Sounds blunt on its own; the normal phrase is 女の人.

ve56a3d0efe.frase: 日本語の先生が変わった。
ve56a3d0efe.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]の 先生[せんせい]が変[か]わった。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

ve56a3d0efe.matiz: Something changes by itself; to change something yourself is 変える. 信号が変わった = the light changed (fun fact: in Japan a green light is called 青, “blue”).

v624b6296e0.frase_furigana: 漢字[かんじ]の 勉強[べんきょう]、大変[たいへん]だね。
v624b6296e0.tono: タイヘン

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v624b6296e0.matiz: 大変[たいへん]だね = “That sounds rough”, a very common sympathetic reply. As a formal adverb it means “very”: 大変[たいへん] 失礼[しつれい]しました (I'm terribly sorry).

v9d78abca9e.frase: 世界で一番大きい国はどこですか。
v9d78abca9e.frase_furigana: 世界[せかい]で 一番[いちばん] 大[おお]きい 国[くに]はどこですか。
v9d78abca9e.frase_es: What's the biggest country in the world?

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v9d78abca9e.matiz: 世界中 = all over the world.

v3850c3cdb4.frase_furigana: どれがあなたの 本[ほん]?

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v3850c3cdb4.matiz: For choosing among three or more. Between two, people prefer どっち or どちら.
v3850c3cdb4.mnemo: The こそあど family: **ど** asks. どれ = **which one?** out of many.

vd114cef4f8.frase_furigana: いい気持[きも]ちですね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vd114cef4f8.matiz: Both mood and physical sensation. 気持ちいい = that feels good; 気持ち悪い = gross, or I feel sick.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence
Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
は: the topic of the sentence

v4a7000d6be.matiz: Going to bed, lying down to sleep. 眠る focuses on the sleep itself, being asleep.

v9087f3e5b5.frase: ニャンは日本で生まれた。
v9087f3e5b5.frase_furigana: ニャンは 日本[にほん]で生[う]まれた。
v9087f3e5b5.tono: ウマレル

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
は: the topic of the sentence

v9087f3e5b5.matiz: Being born (intransitive). Giving birth is 生[う]む or 産[う]む. 1990年[せんきゅうひゃくきゅうじゅうねん]に 生[う]まれた = I was born in 1990.

vbe6454fb71.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]は結婚[けっこん]してる。
vbe6454fb71.tono: ケッコン

gramatica.nota: 結婚している = “to be married”. In speech: 結婚してる.
gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
は: the topic of the sentence

vbe6454fb71.matiz: 結婚する = to get married. “To marry someone” is 〜と結婚する (literally “marry with”), never with を. 結婚している means “to be married”, not “to be getting married”.

v94bf7a7273.frase: ニャンは食べました。それから、寝ました。
v94bf7a7273.frase_furigana: ニャンは 食[た]べました。それから、 寝[ね]ました。
v94bf7a7273.frase_es: Nyan ate. Then he went to sleep.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v950833f54a.frase: おにぎりはいくつありますか。
v950833f54a.frase_furigana: おにぎりはいくつありますか。

gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

v950833f54a.matiz: Also asks someone's age: おいくつですか = How old are you? (polite)

v96b34a1c60.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]が走[はし]ってる。

gramatica.nota: 〜ている = “to be doing something right now”. In speech: 走ってる.
gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v96b34a1c60.matiz: Also for vehicles moving along: 電車[でんしゃ]が 走[はし]る = the train runs; 車[くるま]が 走[はし]る = a car drives along.

v7a295076d9.frase_furigana: 写真[しゃしん]を見[み]せて。
v7a295076d9.matiz: Showing something to someone. Teaching a subject or telling someone a piece of information is 教える, so “show me the way” is 道を教えて.

vb1fa407bdb.frase_furigana: 朝[あさ]は 何[なに]を 食[た]べますか。
vb1fa407bdb.frase_es: What do you eat in the morning?
vb1fa407bdb.matiz: The morning as part of the day. 朝ご飯 = breakfast. 今朝 (けさ) = this morning, with a special reading.

v2cbdefb8d3.frase_furigana: お 父[とう]さん、 何[なに]してる?

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

v2cbdefb8d3.matiz: For calling your own father, or for talking about someone else's.
v2cbdefb8d3.mnemo: Special reading: 父 here is **とう**, not ちち. “**Tou**ché!” shouts **Dad** as he beats you at fencing.

v55d70f776b.frase_furigana: 自転[じてん] 車[しゃ]で 学校[がっこう]に 行[い]く。
v55d70f776b.tono: ジテンシャ
v55d70f776b.frase_es: I go to school by bike.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
で: where an action happens / with what
に: destination, time, where something is

ve326c9eaa1.frase: 日本語がうまいですね。
ve326c9eaa1.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]がうまいですね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

ve326c9eaa1.matiz: More casual than 上手. うまい also means “tasty” (sometimes written 美味い), especially in men's speech. Just like English “good”: good at it, and good to eat.
ve326c9eaa1.mnemo: “**Oo, my**!” gasps the crowd at the **skillful** chef's dish: うまい. (上手 is usually じょうず, but 上手い reads うまい.)

vef2f2dfd2b.frase_furigana: あの女性[じょせい]は 先生[せんせい]です。
vef2f2dfd2b.frase_es: That woman over there is a teacher.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vef2f2dfd2b.matiz: Neutral and slightly formal. Plain 女[おんな] can sound blunt; in conversation, 女[おんな]の 人[ひと] is the normal choice.

v4f35342b0a.frase_furigana: 心[こころ]がきれいな 人[ひと]です。
v4f35342b0a.frase_es: That's a person with a pure heart.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v4f35342b0a.matiz: The heart in the emotional sense, and also the mind. The organ is 心臓. English splits “heart” and “mind”; 心 covers both.

ve36d2a6cd9.frase_furigana: 家族[かぞく]は大切[たいせつ]だよ。
ve36d2a6cd9.tono: タイセツ

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

ve36d2a6cd9.matiz: Almost the same as 大事. 大切にする = to take good care of, cherish: 体を大切にね = take care of yourself.

vbdf2796ef1.frase_furigana: 英語[えいご]と 日本[にほん] 語[ご]を 話[はな]します。

gramatica.nota: と also joins nouns: “X and Y”.
gramatica.titulo: と and や: lists of things

v70c9b46318.frase: ニャンはおにぎりを二つ食べた。
v70c9b46318.frase_furigana: ニャンはおにぎりを二[ふた]つ 食[た]べた。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v70c9b46318.matiz: For counting things: 一つ, 二つ, 三つ… 二つ目 = the second one.

vfc2f186c61.frase: 日本語で百点ぐらい取った。
vfc2f186c61.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]で 百[ひゃく]点[てん]ぐらい 取[と]った。
vfc2f186c61.frase_es: I got about a hundred points in Japanese.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

vfc2f186c61.matiz: Points on a test or in a game: 100点 = a perfect score. Also “respect, aspect”: その点 = in that respect.

v75f911c5a3.tono: シツモン

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

v75f911c5a3.matiz: 質問する = to ask a question. 問題 is a problem or an exercise; 質問 is something someone asks. English “question” covers both.

vaf8fe6332b.matiz: Also for something you both remember: “that thing, you know”. On its own, あれ? = Huh? / Wait, what?
vaf8fe6332b.mnemo: The こそあど family: **あ** is far from both of us. あれ = **that** thing way over there.

v4aa7e9be5e.frase_furigana: 宿題[しゅくだい]、 終[お]わった?
v4aa7e9be5e.tono: シュクダイ

v6dfa23303b.frase_furigana: じゃあ、また 明日[あした]。
v6dfa23303b.matiz: A casual contraction of では. じゃあね = See you!
v6dfa23303b.mnemo: “**Jaa**… **well then**, see ya!” じゃ is just では squished together.

v609c5a6c5e.frase: ニャンは口におにぎりを入れた。
v609c5a6c5e.frase_furigana: ニャンは口[くち]におにぎりを 入[い]れた。
v609c5a6c5e.frase_es: Nyan put an onigiri in his mouth.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v609c5a6c5e.matiz: Also “entrance, exit”: 入口 (entrance), 出口 (exit), where it's read ぐち. 口が悪い = foul-mouthed.

vb4772e805c.frase_furigana: 毎日[まいにち] 日本[にほん] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう]します。
vb4772e805c.matiz: No に: 毎日勉強する. Relative time words (today, tomorrow, every day) take no particle, just as English “every day” needs no “on”.

v1e70f1c0fe.frase: ニャンには長く生きてほしい。
v1e70f1c0fe.frase_furigana: ニャンには 長[なが]く生[い]きてほしい。
v1e70f1c0fe.frase_es: I want Nyan to live a long, long time.

gramatica.nota: Verb て-form + ほしい = wanting someone else to do something: 生きてほしい = “I want (him) to live”.

v1e70f1c0fe.matiz: 生[い]きる is being alive, living your life. Living in a place is 住[す]む: 東京[とうきょう]に 住[す]む. English “live” covers both.

v8d8ccb286a.frase: 関係ないけど、写真を見せてくれない?
v8d8ccb286a.frase_furigana: 関係[かんけい]ないけど、 写真[しゃしん]を 見[み]せてくれない?
v8d8ccb286a.tono: カンケイ
v8d8ccb286a.frase_es: This is random, but could you show me the photo?

gramatica.nota: 〜てくれない? = asking a favor in a friendly way, between friends.
gramatica.titulo: Asking favours, from casual to polite
gramatica.jp: 〜てくれない？・〜てもらえませんか
あげる・くれる・もらう

v8d8ccb286a.matiz: 関係[かんけい]ない said curtly = “None of your business” or “That's got nothing to do with it”. 人間[にんげん] 関係[かんけい] = personal relationships.

v4e2f46de14.frase: 早く始まってほしいですね。
v4e2f46de14.frase_furigana: 早[はや]く始[はじ]まってほしいですね。
v4e2f46de14.tono: ハジマル
v4e2f46de14.frase_es: I hope it starts soon, don't you?
v4e2f46de14.matiz: Something starts: 学校が始まる (school starts). 始まる: something starts on its own. 始める: someone starts something. English uses “start” for both.

v93a1dd8638.frase: バスの時間を教えてくれませんか。
v93a1dd8638.frase_furigana: バスの 時間[じかん]を 教[おし]えてくれませんか。
v93a1dd8638.frase_es: Could you tell me the bus times?

gramatica.jp: あげる・くれる・もらう

v6d0c688c1c.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]は 車[くるま]の下[した]にいます。
v6d0c688c1c.frase_es: The cat is under the car.

gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v6d0c688c1c.matiz: Also “younger, lower”: 下[した]の 子[こ] = the youngest child.

v6b0d133541.frase_furigana: このページを 読[よ]んで。

v2cd9164bbe.frase_furigana: 先生[せんせい]は若[わか]いです。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v2cd9164bbe.matiz: For people and living things; for things that are “new”, use 新しい. 若者 = young people.

ve263fe699f.matiz: Also “very close”: すぐそこ = just over there. すぐに means the same thing.
ve263fe699f.mnemo: Slurp it down in one go: “**Soo-goo**!” That fast: **right away**.

v532cb4ab5b.frase: その本の中で、猫は死ななかった。
v532cb4ab5b.frase_furigana: その 本[ほん]の 中[なか]で、 猫[ねこ]は死[し]ななかった。
v532cb4ab5b.frase_es: In that book, the cat didn't die.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v532cb4ab5b.matiz: The only common verb ending in ぬ: 死にます, 死んだ. Gentler: 亡くなる (to pass away).

v91a034d7da.frase_furigana: 飛行[ひこう] 機[き]で 日本[にほん]に 行[い]きます。

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
に: destination, time, where something is

v6f7f908a8c.frase_furigana: 何[なに]も 食[た]べなかった。
v6f7f908a8c.matiz: Needs a negative verb: 何も食べません = I don't eat anything. English can say “I ate nothing” with a positive verb, but Japanese needs both 何も and the negative.

v3761f07c6d.frase: 父は毎日新聞を読みます。
v3761f07c6d.frase_furigana: 父[ちち]は 毎日[まいにち]新聞[しんぶん]を 読[よ]みます。
v3761f07c6d.tono: シンブン
v3761f07c6d.frase_es: My father reads the newspaper every day.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vd10c0a0454.frase_furigana: 社会[しゃかい]の 先生[せんせい]です。

ve5a24e9352.frase_furigana: きれいな花[はな]ですね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

ve5a24e9352.matiz: Watch out for 鼻 (nose): it's also はな; they're told apart by pitch accent.

v8b47842e14.frase: やっぱり、おにぎりが一番だね。
v8b47842e14.frase_furigana: やっぱり、おにぎりが 一番[いちばん]だね。
v8b47842e14.frase_es: Onigiri really are the best, after all.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v8b47842e14.matiz: Confirms what you already thought, or goes back to an earlier idea: “after all, I knew it”. Also for changing your mind back: やっぱりやめる = actually, never mind. More formal: やはり.

v9545846cf6.frase: 日本語の勉強は楽しいです。
v9545846cf6.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]の 勉強[べんきょう]は楽[たの]しいです。
v9545846cf6.matiz: Fun because you're having a good time. 面白い is fun because it's funny or interesting: a 楽しい party, a 面白い movie.

v95e26dda50.frase_furigana: 今日[きょう]は雨[あめ]ですね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
は: the topic of the sentence

v95e26dda50.matiz: Sounds like 飴 (candy), which has a different pitch. 雨が降る (rain falls) is the set way to say “to rain”.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vcd2f86eedf.matiz: いくら〜ても = no matter how much: いくら 食[た]べても 太[ふと]らない = however much I eat, I don't put on weight.
vcd2f86eedf.mnemo: **Ikura** is salmon roe, the pricey sushi topping: you see it and gasp “**How much**?!” いくら.

vd287eb9b1b.frase: この道を歩いてください。
vd287eb9b1b.frase_furigana: この道[みち]を 歩[ある]いてください。

gramatica.nota: With 歩く, the road you go along takes を.

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

vd287eb9b1b.matiz: Also figurative: the path of an art, where it's read どう: 柔道[じゅうどう] (judo), 茶道[さどう] (the tea ceremony).

v048b52364e.frase: 「いってきます」と言って、家を出ました。
v048b52364e.frase_furigana: 「いってきます」と 言[い]って、 家[いえ]を 出[で]ました。
v048b52364e.tono: イッテキマス
v048b52364e.frase_es: I said “I'm off!” and left the house.
v048b52364e.matiz: Said when leaving home (literally “I'll go and come back”). Whoever stays behind answers いってらっしゃい. English has no fixed pair like this; people just say “Bye!”.

v00900c8b71.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん]の山[やま]は 高[たか]いです。
v00900c8b71.frase_es: The mountains in Japan are high.
v00900c8b71.matiz: Also “a pile, heap”: 山ほどある = there are heaps of them. In mountain names it's read さん: 富士山 (Mount Fuji). Japanese don't say “Fujiyama”.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

va3dc41fbbb.matiz: Intensifies good and bad things alike, the everyday “wow”. すごく + adjective = really, very. Almost always in kana.

v5583fc4747.frase_furigana: 漢字[かんじ]は難[むずか]しいです。
v5583fc4747.tono: ムズカシイ

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v5583fc4747.matiz: The opposite is 易しい or 簡単. As an excuse, それは難しい = “That would be difficult”, which in practice is a polite no.

v4a519eac86.frase_furigana: 先生[せんせい]の 質問[しつもん]に答[こた]える。

gramatica.nota: 答える takes に: 質問に答える.
gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is
Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v4a519eac86.matiz: 答[こた]える is answering a question. Replying to a message or an invitation is usually 返事[へんじ]する.

v66fc84905c.frase: 今日、ニャンは出かけない。
v66fc84905c.frase_furigana: 今日[きょう]、ニャンは出[で]かけない。
v66fc84905c.tono: デカケル

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v66fc84905c.matiz: Leaving home to go somewhere. 出る is leaving any place; 出かける means heading out to do something.

ve2d501370a.frase: ニャンは十時に起きた。
ve2d501370a.frase_furigana: ニャンは 十[じゅう] 時[じ]に起[お]きた。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

ve2d501370a.matiz: Getting up and waking up are both 起[お]きる. It can also mean “to happen”, though for events 起[お]こる is very common too.

v7d28a1869d.frase: 母は「いってらっしゃい」と言いました。
v7d28a1869d.frase_furigana: 母[はは]は「いってらっしゃい」と 言[い]いました。
v7d28a1869d.tono: イッテラッシャイ
v7d28a1869d.matiz: The reply to いってきます, said to someone leaving the house: roughly “go, and come back safe”.

v0ca8800560.frase_furigana: 小[ちい]さい 猫[ねこ]がいる。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v0ca8800560.matiz: Before nouns, 小さな works too.

v4670c2eff8.frase_furigana: 小[ちい]さな 家[いえ]に 住[す]もうと 思[おも]う。
v4670c2eff8.frase_es: I'm thinking of living in a small house.

gramatica.nota: 〜ようと思う = “I'm thinking of doing…”, after the plain volitional (行こう, 住もう).

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v4670c2eff8.matiz: Like 大きな, it only goes before a noun. 小さい works everywhere.

v922160a3ad.frase_furigana: 駅[えき]の近[ちか]くに 住[す]もう。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vba4df65478.frase: 日本語の勉強を続けようと思う。
vba4df65478.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]の 勉強[べんきょう]を続[つづ]けようと 思[おも]う。
vba4df65478.tono: ツヅケル
vba4df65478.frase_es: I'm going to keep studying Japanese.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

vba4df65478.matiz: With another verb's stem: 読み続ける = to keep reading.

v5db93924cd.frase: ニャンは勉強をやめようと思った。
v5db93924cd.frase_furigana: ニャンは 勉強[べんきょう]をやめようと 思[おも]った。
v5db93924cd.frase_es: Nyan thought about giving up studying.

vd6436f98e9.frase_furigana: いい時代[じだい]だったね。
vd6436f98e9.frase_es: Those were the good old days, huh?

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vd6436f98e9.matiz: 学生時代 = your student days. 時代劇 = a samurai period drama. 時代遅れ = out of date.

v6ce946ecba.frase: まず、名前を書いてください。
v6ce946ecba.frase_furigana: まず、 名前[なまえ]を 書[か]いてください。

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

v6ce946ecba.matiz: For putting steps in order: まず〜、 次[つぎ]に〜 = first…, then…
v6ce946ecba.mnemo: “**Ma**, **zoo** **first**, then lunch!” まず = **first of all**.

v325914e12d.frase: ニャンは毎日昼寝をする。
v325914e12d.frase_furigana: ニャンは 毎日[まいにち]昼寝[ひるね]をする。
v325914e12d.frase_es: Nyan takes a nap every day.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
は: the topic of the sentence

v325914e12d.matiz: Nyan's specialty. 昼 (midday) + 寝 (sleep). 昼寝をする = to take a nap.

v7af9491172.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]と犬[いぬ]、どちらが 好[す]き?
