v76c5a61d8d.matiz: To visit a person or a place. Don't confuse it with 尋[たず]ねる (to ask), which sounds the same but is written differently.

ve7d8624c8f.frase: 適当な言葉が見つからないよ。
ve7d8624c8f.frase_furigana: 適当[てきとう]な 言葉[ことば]が 見[み]つからないよ。
ve7d8624c8f.tono: テキトウ
ve7d8624c8f.frase_es: I can't find the right words.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

ve7d8624c8f.matiz: Two faces. Said with care, it means “suitable, appropriate”; said casually, it usually means “sloppy, half-hearted, whatever”: 適当[てきとう]にやる = to do something any old way. Context and tone tell you which.

v4a74d0a98e.frase: 秋が訪れると、空気が冷たくなります。
v4a74d0a98e.frase_furigana: 秋[あき]が訪[おとず]れると、 空気[くうき]が 冷[つめ]たくなります。
v4a74d0a98e.tono: オトズレル
v4a74d0a98e.frase_es: When autumn comes, the air turns cold.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v4a74d0a98e.matiz: More formal and literary than 訪[たず]ねる. It also works for seasons and moments arriving: 春[はる]が訪[おとず]れる = spring arrives.

v8002b7a307.frase: ニャンは雨で濡れちゃったよ。
v8002b7a307.frase_furigana: ニャンは 雨[あめ]で濡[ぬ]れちゃったよ。
v8002b7a307.frase_es: Nyan got soaked in the rain.

gramatica.nota: 濡れてしまった → 濡れちゃった: the casual spoken contraction, used among friends.
gramatica.titulo: 〜てしまう: ending up doing (by accident)
で: where an action happens / with what

v8002b7a307.matiz: Intransitive: clothes or the floor get wet. To make something wet is 濡[ぬ]らす. The cause takes で: 雨[あめ]で濡[ぬ]れる = to get wet in the rain.

v5bd97e6f63.frase: 店で静かな音楽を流しています。
v5bd97e6f63.frase_furigana: 店[みせ]で 静[しず]かな 音楽[おんがく]を流[なが]しています。
v5bd97e6f63.frase_es: They're playing some quiet music in the shop.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
で: where an action happens / with what

v5bd97e6f63.matiz: Transitive partner of 流[なが]れる (to flow): 水[みず]を流[なが]す = to run the water, or to flush the toilet. Also for playing background music in a place, where English just says “play”.

v5b6cfc8775.frase: 家族は田舎に住んでいます。
v5b6cfc8775.frase_furigana: 家族[かぞく]は田舎[いなか]に 住[す]んでいます。
v5b6cfc8775.frase_es: My family lives in the countryside.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
に: destination, time, where something is

v5b6cfc8775.matiz: The opposite of the city. It can also mean your hometown, said with affection, a bit like “back home”: 田舎[いなか]に帰[かえ]る = to go back home.

v6399cdfe32.frase: 車のエンジンが動きません。
v6399cdfe32.frase_furigana: 車[くるま]のエンジンが 動[うご]きません。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

vda1acc7d71.frase: 悪いニュースはすぐに広がります。
vda1acc7d71.frase_furigana: 悪[わる]いニュースはすぐに広[ひろ]がります。
vda1acc7d71.tono: ヒロガル

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vda1acc7d71.matiz: Intransitive: a fire, a rumor or a view spreads out by itself. The transitive partner is 広[ひろ]げる (to spread something out).

ve047c54d5b.frase: 喫茶店でコーヒーを飲みました。
ve047c54d5b.frase_furigana: 喫茶[きっさ] 店[てん]でコーヒーを 飲[の]みました。
ve047c54d5b.tono: キッサテン
ve047c54d5b.frase_es: I had a coffee at a coffee shop.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

ve047c54d5b.matiz: A classic, old-style Japanese coffee shop. A modern chain is usually called カフェ.

v31ff9fa7f3.matiz: Childlike or affectionate, like “daddy”. The general word is お父[とう]さん.

v092e6aa260.frase: この町にはお寺がたくさんあります。
v092e6aa260.frase_furigana: この 町[まち]にはお寺[てら]がたくさんあります。
v092e6aa260.frase_es: There are lots of temples in this town.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v092e6aa260.matiz: A Buddhist temple. A Shinto shrine is 神社[じんじゃ]. In speech it's usually お寺[てら]; at the end of a temple's name it's read じ: 金閣寺[きんかくじ].

ve6d74efad1.frase_furigana: コップに 水[みず]を 入[い]れて。
ve6d74efad1.frase_es: Put some water in the glass.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

ve6d74efad1.matiz: Despite the sound, it's a drinking glass or tumbler, usually for cold drinks. For hot coffee or tea, カップ is more common. A paper cup is 紙[かみ]コップ.

v8dd19da7a6.frase: その話は先生に直接聞いて。
v8dd19da7a6.frase_furigana: その 話[はなし]は 先生[せんせい]に直接[ちょくせつ] 聞[き]いて。
v8dd19da7a6.tono: チョクセツ
v8dd19da7a6.frase_es: Ask the teacher about that directly.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is
は: the topic of the sentence

v8dd19da7a6.matiz: The opposite is 間接[かんせつ] (indirect). 直接[ちょくせつ]話[はな]す = to talk in person, with no one in between.

v54e98ecede.frase: 私はアルコールを飲みません。
v54e98ecede.frase_furigana: 私[わたし]はアルコールを 飲[の]みません。
v54e98ecede.tono: アルコール

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v54e98ecede.matiz: Covers both the substance and alcoholic drinks in general, as in English. In everyday talk, お酒[さけ] is the more common word for drinks.

v6cc619d46c.frase: ニャンは我慢して勉強してるよ。
v6cc619d46c.frase_furigana: ニャンは我慢[がまん]して 勉強[べんきょう]してるよ。
v6cc619d46c.frase_es: Nyan is sticking it out and studying.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v6cc619d46c.matiz: 我慢[がまん]する = to put up with something, to hold yourself back: 我慢[がまん]できない = I can't take it anymore.

v724b064b58.frase: やっと電話がつながったよ！
v724b064b58.frase_furigana: やっと 電話[でんわ]がつながったよ！
v724b064b58.tono: ツナガル

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v724b064b58.matiz: For the internet, a phone line or two places: つながる means they end up connected. 電話[でんわ]がつながる = the call goes through. The transitive partner is つなぐ (to connect something).

v1227aee25f.frase: 明日までにレポートを出さなきゃ。
v1227aee25f.frase_furigana: 明日[あした]までにレポートを 出[だ]さなきゃ。
v1227aee25f.frase_es: I've got to hand in my paper by tomorrow.

gramatica.nota: 出さなければならない → 出さなきゃ: the casual spoken short form of “have to”, used among friends.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v1227aee25f.matiz: A written assignment for school or university, what English calls a paper or an essay. A business report is usually 報告書[ほうこくしょ].

ve67bdf1dd7.frase: 彼はいつも丁寧に話します。
ve67bdf1dd7.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]はいつも丁寧[ていねい]に 話[はな]します。
ve67bdf1dd7.matiz: Covers both good manners and careful work: 丁寧[ていねい]に書[か]く = to write neatly and carefully. 丁寧語[ていねいご] is the polite です/ます style.

v5ff0c9cc43.frase: 部屋をきちんと掃除してほしいな。
v5ff0c9cc43.frase_furigana: 部屋[へや]をきちんと 掃除[そうじ]してほしいな。
v5ff0c9cc43.frase_es: I'd like you to clean your room properly.

gramatica.nota: 〜てほしい: wanting someone else to do something, softer than ください. 掃除してほしい = “I'd like you to clean”.

v5ff0c9cc43.matiz: Doing something properly and neatly, the way it should be done, with nothing out of place: 部屋[へや]をきちんと掃除[そうじ]する. ちゃんと means much the same but is more casual.

v6bb38fe69d.frase: ニャンは勝手にベッドで寝たよ。
v6bb38fe69d.frase_furigana: ニャンは勝手[かって]にベッドで 寝[ね]たよ。
v6bb38fe69d.frase_es: Nyan went and slept on the bed without asking.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v6bb38fe69d.matiz: 勝手[かって]に = on your own, without asking anyone: 勝手[かって]に使[つか]わないで = don't use it without asking. 勝手[かって]な人[ひと] = a selfish person.

v39e0b53ee8.frase: 駅で切符を買いました。
v39e0b53ee8.frase_furigana: 駅[えき]で切符[きっぷ]を 買[か]いました。
v39e0b53ee8.frase_es: I bought a ticket at the station.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v39e0b53ee8.matiz: A ticket for a train or bus. For movies or concerts, use チケット.

v8c79b968f6.frase: このデパートの地下に店があります。
v8c79b968f6.frase_furigana: このデパートの地下[ちか]に 店[みせ]があります。
v8c79b968f6.frase_es: There are shops in the basement of this department store.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v8c79b968f6.matiz: 地下鉄[ちかてつ] = the subway (literally “underground railway”). 地下[ちか]一階[いっかい] = the first basement floor, B1 in an elevator.

v78da824a5a.frase: この機械の使い方がわかりません。
v78da824a5a.frase_furigana: この機械[きかい]の 使[つか]い 方[かた]がわかりません。
v78da824a5a.frase_es: I don't know how to use this machine.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v78da824a5a.matiz: Machines and equipment in general. Don't mix it up with 機会[きかい] (chance, opportunity), which sounds exactly the same.

v83b9451def.frase: ニャンはお金持ちになりたいよ。
v83b9451def.frase_furigana: ニャンはお 金持[かねも]ちになりたいよ。
v83b9451def.tono: オカネモチ

gramatica.titulo: になる (to become) and にする (to decide, to make)
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v83b9451def.matiz: From お金[かね] (money) + 持[も]つ (to have): literally “someone who has money”. Japanese uses this noun where English says “rich”: お金持[かねも]ちになる = to get rich.

v12a0b5619b.frase: 海岸を散歩するのが好きです。
v12a0b5619b.frase_furigana: 海岸[かいがん]を 散歩[さんぽ]するのが 好[す]きです。
v12a0b5619b.tono: カイガン
v12a0b5619b.frase_es: I like walking along the coast.

gramatica.titulo: Turning an action into a noun
Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v12a0b5619b.matiz: The coast or shoreline in general. A sandy beach where people swim is 浜[はま] or ビーチ.

ve4fb985ca8.frase: 最後に一言お願いします。
ve4fb985ca8.frase_furigana: 最後[さいご]に一言[ひとこと]お 願[ねが]いします。
ve4fb985ca8.frase_es: And finally, could you say a few words?

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

ve4fb985ca8.matiz: Literally “one word”, but it means a short remark: 一言[ひとこと]どうぞ = please say a few words. 一言[ひとこと]で言[い]うと = in a word.

v7ddbc5fc2c.frase: 彼から何も反応がありませんでした。
v7ddbc5fc2c.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]から 何[なに]も反応[はんのう]がありませんでした。
v7ddbc5fc2c.tono: ハンノウ
v7ddbc5fc2c.frase_es: I got no response from him at all.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v7ddbc5fc2c.matiz: 反応[はんのう]する = to react. いい反応[はんのう]がない = the response isn't good.

v484dccc50f.frase: 子供の頃、宇宙に興味がありました。
v484dccc50f.frase_furigana: 子供[こども]の 頃[ころ]、宇宙[うちゅう]に 興味[きょうみ]がありました。
v484dccc50f.frase_es: When I was a kid, I was interested in space.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

v484dccc50f.matiz: One word for both “space” and “the universe”. 宇宙人[うちゅうじん] = an alien (literally “space person”). 宇宙[うちゅう]に行[い]く = to go to space.

ve859a55c60.frase: 私はあのチームのファンだよ。
ve859a55c60.frase_furigana: 私[わたし]はあのチームのファンだよ。
ve859a55c60.frase_es: I'm a fan of that team.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

ve859a55c60.matiz: A fan of a singer, a team or a show. It's never the machine that cools you: an electric fan is 扇風機[せんぷうき].

vc4742268a1.frase: ニャンはリンゴよりおにぎりが好きだよ。
vc4742268a1.frase_furigana: ニャンはリンゴよりおにぎりが 好[す]きだよ。
vc4742268a1.frase_es: Nyan likes onigiri more than apples.

gramatica.titulo: Liking and being good at: が with adjectives

v39d849cc18.frase: わずかな時間で終わりました。
v39d849cc18.frase_furigana: わずかな 時間[じかん]で 終[お]わりました。
v39d849cc18.frase_es: It was over in no time at all.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v39d849cc18.matiz: A very small amount, next to nothing: わずかな時間[じかん] = very little time. Before numbers it means “a mere”: わずか三日[みっか] = just three days.

v2c2e7bed70.frase: 二人、三年前から付き合ってるよ。
v2c2e7bed70.frase_furigana: 二人[ふたり]、 三[さん] 年[ねん] 前[まえ]から付[つ]き 合[あ]ってるよ。
v2c2e7bed70.frase_es: Those two have been going out for three years.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

v2c2e7bed70.matiz: As a couple: 三年[さんねん]付[つ]き合[あ]っています = we've been dating for three years. It also means keeping someone company: 買[か]い物[もの]に付[つ]き合[あ]う = to go shopping with someone.

v8037127ec1.frase: ニャンはなかなか部屋を片付けないよ。
v8037127ec1.frase_furigana: ニャンはなかなか 部屋[へや]を片付[かたづ]けないよ。
v8037127ec1.tono: カタヅケル
v8037127ec1.frase_es: Nyan just won't tidy his room.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v8037127ec1.matiz: To tidy up and put things back where they belong: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]を片付[かたづ]ける = to clear off the desk. It's about order rather than dirt; cleaning is 掃除[そうじ].

vd5b2b837d4.frase: ニャンと一緒に何か食おうよ。
vd5b2b837d4.frase_furigana: ニャンと 一緒[いっしょ]に 何[なに]か食[く]おうよ。
vd5b2b837d4.frase_es: Let's grab something to eat with Nyan!

gramatica.titulo: と and や: lists of things
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vd5b2b837d4.matiz: A blunt, masculine version of 食[た]べる, used among friends: 食[く]わない, 食[く]おう. A bit like “chow down”. Stick with 食[た]べる when you're being polite.

vd78d407d5e.frase: 自由な時間が減りました。
vd78d407d5e.frase_furigana: 自由[じゆう]な 時間[じかん]が減[へ]りました。
vd78d407d5e.frase_es: I have less free time now.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

vd78d407d5e.matiz: Intransitive: an amount goes down by itself. The transitive partner is 減[へ]らす (to reduce). お腹[なか]が減[へ]る = to get hungry.

v44bb932305.frase_furigana: 寒[さむ]いから上着[うわぎ] 着[き]て。
v44bb932305.frase_es: It's cold, so put on a jacket.

gramatica.titulo: から and ので: because

v44bb932305.matiz: Whatever you wear on top, a jacket or a coat. Underwear is 下着[したぎ].

v63040d51c0.frase: あの夫婦は公園を散歩しています。
v63040d51c0.frase_furigana: あの夫婦[ふうふ]は 公園[こうえん]を 散歩[さんぽ]しています。
v63040d51c0.frase_es: That couple is taking a walk in the park.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

v63040d51c0.matiz: The couple as a unit, literally “husband + wife”: あの夫婦[ふうふ] = that married couple.

vb705d40674.frase: 教室で実験をしました。
vb705d40674.frase_furigana: 教室[きょうしつ]で実験[じっけん]をしました。
vb705d40674.tono: ジッケン
vb705d40674.frase_es: We did an experiment in the classroom.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

vb705d40674.matiz: 実験[じっけん]する = to do an experiment.

v52489aaa8d.frase: あの角を右に曲がって。
v52489aaa8d.frase_furigana: あの角[かど]を 右[みぎ]に 曲[ま]がって。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v52489aaa8d.matiz: The corner of a street or an object: あの角[かど]を曲[ま]がってください = please turn at that corner. Read つの, the same kanji means “horn”.

vade21c1bbb.frase: この機械は丁寧に扱ってください。
vade21c1bbb.frase_furigana: この 機械[きかい]は 丁寧[ていねい]に扱[あつか]ってください。
vade21c1bbb.tono: アツカウ
vade21c1bbb.frase_es: Please handle this machine with care.

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

vade21c1bbb.matiz: For handling objects, dealing with cases or treating people: 子供[こども]として扱[あつか]う = to treat someone like a child.

v83fef172ad.frase: 鍵を右に回してくれない？
v83fef172ad.frase_furigana: 鍵[かぎ]を 右[みぎ]に回[まわ]してくれない？
v83fef172ad.frase_es: Can you turn the key to the right?

gramatica.nota: 〜てくれない？: asking a friend for a favor, softer than ください. 回してくれない？ = “could you turn it?”
gramatica.titulo: Asking favours, from casual to polite
gramatica.jp: 〜てくれない？・〜てもらえませんか
あげる・くれる・もらう

v83fef172ad.matiz: Transitive partner of 回[まわ]る (to turn, to spin): 鍵[かぎ]を回[まわ]す = to turn the key.

v617fca27c3.frase: ニャンはおにぎりを隠してるよ。
v617fca27c3.frase_furigana: ニャンはおにぎりを隠[かく]してるよ。

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v617fca27c3.matiz: To hide an object or a feeling: 気持[きも]ちを隠[かく]す = to hide your feelings. Hiding yourself is 隠[かく]れる.

v14aa0e8f7c.frase: ケーキを二つに分けたよ。
v14aa0e8f7c.frase_furigana: ケーキを 二[ふた]つに分[わ]けたよ。
v14aa0e8f7c.frase_es: I cut the cake in two.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
に: destination, time, where something is

v14aa0e8f7c.matiz: To split something into parts: ケーキを半分[はんぶん]に分[わ]ける = to cut the cake in half. The parts take に.

v6cfd818538.frase: 先生の作品を拝見して比較しました。
v6cfd818538.frase_furigana: 先生[せんせい]の 作品[さくひん]を 拝見[はいけん]して比較[ひかく]しました。
v6cfd818538.frase_es: I took a respectful look at the teacher's work and compared it.
v6cfd818538.matiz: 比較[ひかく]する = to compare, a bit formal. In everyday speech 比[くら]べる is more common: 〜に比[くら]べて = compared with…

v2d998c292a.frase: 椅子を動かして、報告いたします。
v2d998c292a.frase_furigana: 椅子[いす]を動[うご]かして、 報告[ほうこく]いたします。
v2d998c292a.frase_es: I will move the chair and report back to you.

gramatica.nota: 致[いた]す is the humble form of する: 報告いたします makes the speaker humble, out of respect for the listener.

v2d998c292a.matiz: Transitive partner of 動[うご]く (to move): 機械[きかい]を動[うご]かす = to start up a machine. English “move” works both ways; Japanese splits it into 動く (something moves) and 動かす (you move something).

vb722c9019c.frase: 警官が「気をつけてください」とおっしゃいました。
vb722c9019c.frase_furigana: 警官[けいかん]が「 気[き]をつけてください」とおっしゃいました。
vb722c9019c.tono: ケイカン
vb722c9019c.frase_es: The police officer said, “Please be careful.”

gramatica.nota: おっしゃる is the respectful form of 言う: for what someone else says, never for yourself.

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

vb722c9019c.matiz: More formal than お巡[まわ]りさん, the friendly everyday word. The police as an organization is 警察[けいさつ].

vd365e2d430.frase: 来週、他の学校の先生が訪問にいらっしゃいます。
vd365e2d430.frase_furigana: 来週[らいしゅう]、 他[た]の 学校[がっこう]の 先生[せんせい]が訪問[ほうもん]にいらっしゃいます。
vd365e2d430.tono: ホウモン
vd365e2d430.frase_es: Next week, a teacher from another school is coming to visit.

gramatica.nota: いらっしゃる replaces 来る, 行く and いる when you talk about someone you respect. Here it means “will come”.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
に: destination, time, where something is

vd365e2d430.matiz: More formal than 訪[たず]ねる: used for official or business visits. 訪問[ほうもん]する = to pay a visit.

ve7d168fbba.frase: この味噌を召し上がったことがありますか。
ve7d168fbba.frase_furigana: この味噌[みそ]を 召[め]し 上[あ]がったことがありますか。
ve7d168fbba.frase_es: Have you ever tried this miso?

gramatica.nota: 召し上がる is the respectful form of 食べる and 飲む: for what someone else eats or drinks.

gramatica.titulo: Generic nouns: こと, ところ, もの

ve7d168fbba.matiz: A basic Japanese ingredient made from fermented soybeans. Stirred into hot broth, it becomes 味噌汁[みそしる] (miso soup).

v3dcb0ed7db.frase: ニャンはおにぎりを袋に入れたよ。
v3dcb0ed7db.frase_furigana: ニャンはおにぎりを袋[ふくろ]に 入[い]れたよ。
v3dcb0ed7db.frase_es: Nyan put the onigiri in a bag.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
に: destination, time, where something is

v3dcb0ed7db.matiz: A paper or plastic bag. A bag you carry around, like a schoolbag or briefcase, is かばん, and a handbag is バッグ. At the checkout: 袋[ふくろ]はいりますか = Do you need a bag?

v3b192941aa.frase: 川の流れがとても速いです。
v3b192941aa.frase_furigana: 川[かわ]の流[なが]れがとても 速[はや]いです。
v3b192941aa.frase_es: The river's current is very fast.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v3b192941aa.matiz: The noun form of 流[なが]れる (to flow): 川[かわ]の流[なが]れ = the river's current; 話[はなし]の流[なが]れ = the flow of a conversation.

v84c8f9983b.frase: 地図で今の位置を確認しました。
v84c8f9983b.frase_furigana: 地図[ちず]で 今[いま]の位置[いち]を 確認[かくにん]しました。
v84c8f9983b.frase_es: I checked my current position on the map.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v84c8f9983b.matiz: 位置[いち]する = to be located. On a map app, your current location is 現在地[げんざいち].

v6734f4c192.frase: 女子チームが試合に勝ったよ！
v6734f4c192.frase_furigana: 女子[じょし]チームが 試合[しあい]に 勝[か]ったよ！
v6734f4c192.frase_es: The girls' team won the game!

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v6734f4c192.matiz: Used for groups and categories: 女子[じょし]チーム = the girls' or women's team; 女子[じょし]トイレ = the women's restroom. One girl is 女[おんな]の子[こ]. The male counterpart is 男子[だんし].

v163a461d3f.frase: ニャンは朝ご飯を抜かなかったよ。
v163a461d3f.frase_furigana: ニャンは 朝[あさ]ご 飯[はん]を抜[ぬ]かなかったよ。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v163a461d3f.matiz: To take something out of where it was: 歯[は]を抜[ぬ]く = to pull a tooth. Also leaving something out: 朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]を抜[ぬ]く = to skip breakfast.

ve0d9257941.frase: ご出身はどちらですか。
ve0d9257941.frase_furigana: ご出身[しゅっしん]はどちらですか。
ve0d9257941.tono: シュッシン

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

ve0d9257941.matiz: ご出身[しゅっしん]はどちらですか is the classic polite way to ask “Where are you from?”. It also covers your school: 東京[とうきょう]大学[だいがく]出身[しゅっしん] = a University of Tokyo graduate.

v3afd1682f2.frase: 毎年、家族と神社に伺います。
v3afd1682f2.frase_furigana: 毎年[まいとし]、 家族[かぞく]と神社[じんじゃ]に 伺[うかが]います。
v3afd1682f2.frase_es: Every year, I visit the shrine with my family.

gramatica.nota: 伺う is the humble form of 行く: here, paying a respectful visit to a place.

gramatica.titulo: と and や: lists of things
に: destination, time, where something is

v3afd1682f2.matiz: A Shinto shrine, with a red torii gate at the entrance. A Buddhist temple is お寺[てら].

v4f895e5e1a.frase: その服、とても素敵だね。
v4f895e5e1a.frase_furigana: その 服[ふく]、とても素敵[すてき]だね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v4f895e5e1a.matiz: A go-to compliment for clothes, places or people: 素敵[すてき]な服[ふく]ですね = what a lovely outfit.

vb92836ba69.frase_furigana: 答[こた]えを当[あ]ててみて。
vb92836ba69.matiz: To guess something right: 答[こた]えを当[あ]てる. It also means to hit a target, or to hold something against something: 氷[こおり]を当[あ]てる = to put ice on it.

va56230b4d8.frase: 彼女は医者を目指しています。
va56230b4d8.frase_furigana: 彼女[かのじょ]は 医者[いしゃ]を目指[めざ]しています。
va56230b4d8.frase_es: She's aiming to become a doctor.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

va56230b4d8.matiz: To have something as your goal: 医者[いしゃ]を目指[めざ]す = to aim to become a doctor. Japanese just names the goal, where English adds “to become”.

v8e854a88d7.frase_furigana: 会場[かいじょう]はどちらですか。
v8e854a88d7.tono: カイジョウ

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v8e854a88d7.matiz: The place where an event is held: コンサート会場[かいじょう] = the concert venue.

vb1987f1b95.frase: この病気は治療が必要です。
vb1987f1b95.frase_furigana: この 病気[びょうき]は治療[ちりょう]が 必要[ひつよう]です。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
は: the topic of the sentence

vb1987f1b95.matiz: Medical treatment. 治療[ちりょう]する = to treat an illness or injury. Don't mix it up with 治[なお]す, the everyday verb for curing or fixing anything.

v197c1d4e58.frase: その着物、とても素敵だね。
v197c1d4e58.frase_furigana: その着物[きもの]、とても 素敵[すてき]だね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v197c1d4e58.matiz: Literally “thing to wear”. It can mean any traditional Japanese clothing; Western-style clothes are 洋服[ようふく].

v89eda0dba6.frase: この本を日本語に翻訳しました。
v89eda0dba6.frase_furigana: この 本[ほん]を 日本[にほん] 語[ご]に翻訳[ほんやく]しました。
v89eda0dba6.tono: ホンヤク
v89eda0dba6.frase_es: I translated this book into Japanese.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v89eda0dba6.matiz: 翻訳[ほんやく]する = to translate written text. Interpreting speech out loud is 通訳[つうやく]. The language you translate into takes に.

v223d115459.frase: ニャンはおにぎりを手でつかんだよ。
v223d115459.frase_furigana: ニャンはおにぎりを 手[て]でつかんだよ。
v223d115459.frase_es: Nyan grabbed the onigiri with his paw.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v223d115459.matiz: To grab hold of something firmly: 手[て]をつかむ = to grab someone's hand. As in English, you can also grasp a chance: チャンスをつかむ = to seize the chance.

vf0edddb6f4.frase: 昨日、駅で先生を見かけました。
vf0edddb6f4.frase_furigana: 昨日[きのう]、 駅[えき]で 先生[せんせい]を見[み]かけました。
vf0edddb6f4.tono: ミカケル
vf0edddb6f4.frase_es: I happened to see my teacher at the station yesterday.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

vf0edddb6f4.matiz: To see someone in passing, without looking for them: 駅[えき]で友達[ともだち]を見[み]かけました = I spotted a friend at the station. If you actually meet and talk, it's 会[あ]う.

v404e68abe1.frase_furigana: 髪[かみ]を伸[の]ばしてるよ。

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v404e68abe1.matiz: Transitive partner of 伸[の]びる (to grow, to stretch): 髪[かみ]を伸[の]ばす = to grow your hair out; 手[て]を伸[の]ばす = to reach out your hand.

v534e72b8d7.frase: ニャンはお昼を食べて寝たよ。
v534e72b8d7.frase_furigana: ニャンはお 昼[ひる]を 食[た]べて 寝[ね]たよ。
v534e72b8d7.frase_es: Nyan ate lunch and went to sleep.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v534e72b8d7.matiz: It also means lunch itself: お昼[ひる]を食[た]べる = to have lunch. A softer, everyday alternative to 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん].

ve1382dfcc6.frase: 祖父は今年80歳になりました。
ve1382dfcc6.frase_furigana: 祖父[そふ]は 今年[ことし]80 歳[さい]になりました。

gramatica.titulo: になる (to become) and にする (to decide, to make)

ve1382dfcc6.matiz: For talking about your own grandfather to people outside the family. To address him, or to talk about someone else's grandfather, use おじいさん.

v38b346ee2f.frase: 祖母は料理がとても上手だよ。
v38b346ee2f.frase_furigana: 祖母[そぼ]は 料理[りょうり]がとても 上手[じょうず]だよ。
v38b346ee2f.frase_es: My grandmother is a really good cook.

gramatica.titulo: Liking and being good at: が with adjectives
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v38b346ee2f.matiz: For talking about your own grandmother to people outside the family. To address her, or to talk about someone else's grandmother, use おばあさん.

va42d5af3fb.frase: 神社でみんなの幸せを祈りました。
va42d5af3fb.frase_furigana: 神社[じんじゃ]でみんなの 幸[しあわ]せを祈[いの]りました。
va42d5af3fb.frase_es: At the shrine, I prayed for everyone's happiness.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

va42d5af3fb.matiz: Praying at a temple or shrine, or wishing for something with all your heart: 幸[しあわ]せを祈[いの]る = to pray for someone's happiness.

va80fea82b3.frase: 人が多い時間は避けるよ。
va80fea82b3.frase_furigana: 人[ひと]が 多[おお]い 時間[じかん]は避[さ]けるよ。
va80fea82b3.frase_es: I avoid the times when it's crowded.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

va80fea82b3.matiz: To avoid something or someone: 人[ひと]を避[さ]ける = to avoid a person.

vd0c87670ff.frase: 先週、美術館に行きました。
vd0c87670ff.frase_furigana: 先週[せんしゅう]、美術[びじゅつ] 館[かん]に 行[い]きました。
vd0c87670ff.tono: ビジュツカン
vd0c87670ff.frase_es: I went to an art museum last week.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vd0c87670ff.matiz: 美術[びじゅつ] (art) + 館[かん] (building). A general museum, like a history or science museum, is 博物館[はくぶつかん].

vb4dc2b1a78.frase_furigana: 今[いま]、 家[いえ]は留守[るす]です。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vb4dc2b1a78.matiz: 留守[るす]にする = to be out, away from home. 留守番[るすばん] = staying home to mind the house while others are out.

vbb68132c58.frase: このシャツのサイズが合いません。
vbb68132c58.frase_furigana: このシャツのサイズが 合[あ]いません。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

vbb68132c58.matiz: Clothing sizes or size in general: サイズが合[あ]わない = it's the wrong size, it doesn't fit.

v85f644fa90.frase: 先輩に日本語を教えてもらいました。
v85f644fa90.frase_furigana: 先輩[せんぱい]に 日本[にほん] 語[ご]を 教[おし]えてもらいました。
v85f644fa90.tono: センパイ
v85f644fa90.frase_es: One of my seniors taught me Japanese.

gramatica.jp: あげる・くれる・もらう

v85f644fa90.matiz: Someone who started before you at school or work: an upperclassman or a more senior colleague. The opposite is 後輩[こうはい]. It's also used as a title after a name: 田中[たなか]先輩[せんぱい].

v28f5d53714.frase: いい体験になりました。
v28f5d53714.frase_furigana: いい体験[たいけん]になりました。
v28f5d53714.tono: タイケン

gramatica.titulo: になる (to become) and にする (to decide, to make)

v28f5d53714.matiz: Something you live through yourself: いい体験[たいけん]になりました = it turned out to be a good experience. 体験[たいけん]する = to experience, to try out.

vad2fc89ba4.frase_furigana: 石鹸[せっけん]で 手[て]を 洗[あら]って。
vad2fc89ba4.tono: セッケン

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

vc47d476599.frase: 日本語にまだ自信がないよ。
vc47d476599.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]にまだ自信[じしん]がないよ。
vc47d476599.frase_es: I'm still not confident in my Japanese.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

vc47d476599.matiz: 自信[じしん]がある / ない = to be confident or not. Don't confuse it with 地震[じしん] (earthquake), which sounds exactly the same.

v2db48ab9a2.frase: ニャンは布団から出たくないよ。
v2db48ab9a2.frase_furigana: ニャンは布団[ふとん]から 出[で]たくないよ。
v2db48ab9a2.frase_es: Nyan doesn't want to get out of his futon.
v2db48ab9a2.matiz: The Japanese mattress and quilt you lay out on the floor to sleep on, then fold away in the morning. Not the Western futon sofa bed.

v8668714cf6.frase: 廊下を走らないでください。
v8668714cf6.frase_furigana: 廊下[ろうか]を 走[はし]らないでください。
v8668714cf6.frase_es: Please don't run in the hallway.

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください

v71da0f1a83.frase_furigana: 毎週[まいしゅう]、 神社[じんじゃ]に 伺[うかが]っています。
v71da0f1a83.tono: マイシュウ
v71da0f1a83.frase_es: I visit the shrine every week.

gramatica.nota: 伺う again: the humble form of 行く, for going somewhere respectfully.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

vd935972262.frase_furigana: この 時計[とけい]は正確[せいかく]です。
vd935972262.tono: セイカク

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vd935972262.matiz: Don't confuse it with 性格[せいかく] (personality), which sounds exactly the same but uses different kanji.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

ve83e2537d2.frase: みんなで協力しようよ。
ve83e2537d2.frase_furigana: みんなで協力[きょうりょく]しようよ。
ve83e2537d2.tono: キョウリョク
ve83e2537d2.frase_es: Come on, let's all work together.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

ve83e2537d2.matiz: 協力[きょうりょく]する = to cooperate, to work together. Signs and announcements often say ご協力[きょうりょく]をお願[ねが]いします: “we appreciate your cooperation”.

v8e6d569a40.frase: ニャンはなかなか集中できないよ。
v8e6d569a40.frase_furigana: ニャンはなかなか集中[しゅうちゅう]できないよ。
v8e6d569a40.tono: シュウチュウ
v8e6d569a40.frase_es: Nyan has a hard time concentrating.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
は: the topic of the sentence

v8e6d569a40.matiz: 集中[しゅうちゅう]する = to concentrate, to focus.

v6ef6d5e856.frase_furigana: 再[ふたた]び 会[あ]えてうれしいよ。
v6ef6d5e856.tono: フタタビ
v6ef6d5e856.frase_es: I'm so happy to see you again.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v6ef6d5e856.matiz: More formal and literary than また, like English “once again”: 再[ふたた]び会[あ]いましょう = let us meet again.

v70333cb82f.frase_furigana: いろんな 人[ひと]に 会[あ]ったよ。
v70333cb82f.tono: イロンナ
v70333cb82f.frase_es: I met all kinds of people.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
に: destination, time, where something is

v70333cb82f.matiz: The casual form of いろいろな: いろんな人[ひと]がいます = there are all kinds of people.

v608c04966f.frase: 洗濯物がもう乾きました。
v608c04966f.frase_furigana: 洗濯物[せんたくもの]がもう乾[かわ]きました。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v608c04966f.matiz: Intransitive: clothes dry by themselves. To dry something is 乾[かわ]かす. Being thirsty, 喉[のど]が渇[かわ]く, sounds the same but uses a different kanji.

vf3b624cb18.frase: 友達と本を交換しました。
vf3b624cb18.frase_furigana: 友達[ともだち]と 本[ほん]を交換[こうかん]しました。
vf3b624cb18.tono: コウカン
vf3b624cb18.frase_es: I swapped books with a friend.

gramatica.titulo: と and や: lists of things

vf3b624cb18.matiz: 交換[こうかん]する = to exchange, to swap. Also for replacing a part: 電池[でんち]を交換[こうかん]する = to change the batteries.

v61f7d11712.frase: この本を参考にしました。
v61f7d11712.frase_furigana: この 本[ほん]を参考[さんこう]にしました。
v61f7d11712.tono: サンコウ
v61f7d11712.frase_es: I used this book as a reference.

gramatica.titulo: になる (to become) and にする (to decide, to make)

v61f7d11712.matiz: 参考[さんこう]にする = to use something as a reference. 参考[さんこう]になる = to be helpful or informative: とても参考[さんこう]になりました = that was really helpful.

v0cd013cc34.frase: たとえ雨が降っても行くよ。
v0cd013cc34.frase_furigana: たとえ 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]っても 行[い]くよ。
v0cd013cc34.frase_es: I'm going even if it rains.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v0cd013cc34.matiz: It comes with 〜ても and makes the “even if” stronger: たとえ雨[あめ]が降[ふ]っても行[い]きます = I'll go even if it rains.

vdb47a7f849.frase: 日本にいいイメージがあります。
vdb47a7f849.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん]にいいイメージがあります。
vdb47a7f849.frase_es: I have a good impression of Japan.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

vdb47a7f849.matiz: The image or impression something gives you, the picture in your head: いいイメージがあります. イメージする = to picture, to imagine.

v7b4395a049.frase: ニャンはいつも道に迷うよ。
v7b4395a049.frase_furigana: ニャンはいつも 道[みち]に迷[まよ]うよ。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence
に: destination, time, where something is

v7b4395a049.matiz: Two kinds of lost: lost on the road, 道[みち]に迷[まよ]う, and lost between choices: どれにするか迷[まよ]う = I can't decide which one to pick.

v2ba57e9474.frase: あらゆる人がここに来ます。
v2ba57e9474.frase_furigana: あらゆる 人[ひと]がここに 来[き]ます。
v2ba57e9474.frase_es: All kinds of people come here.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
に: destination, time, where something is

v2ba57e9474.matiz: Always comes right before a noun, and sounds formal: あらゆる方法[ほうほう]を試[ため]しました = I tried every possible way.

v72992d8977.frase: ニャンは床で寝てるよ。
v72992d8977.frase_furigana: ニャンは床[ゆか]で 寝[ね]てるよ。
v72992d8977.frase_es: Nyan is sleeping on the floor.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v72992d8977.matiz: The floor of a room, usually wooden. The ground outside is 地面[じめん].

v4e1c545daf.frase_furigana: 電車[でんしゃ]で移動[いどう]したよ。

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v4e1c545daf.matiz: 移動[いどう]する = to move from one place to another, to get around: 電車[でんしゃ]で移動[いどう]する = to travel by train. It's never moving house; that's 引[ひ]っ越[こ]す.

v28a392a583.frase: 来月、新しい部屋に移ります。
v28a392a583.frase_furigana: 来月[らいげつ]、 新[あたら]しい 部屋[へや]に移[うつ]ります。
v28a392a583.frase_es: I'm moving into a new room next month.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v28a392a583.matiz: Intransitive: you move, or something passes to another place. The transitive partner is 移[うつ]す. A cold can move too: 風邪[かぜ]がうつる = to catch a cold from someone.

vc141fa938a.frase: この町には魅力があります。
vc141fa938a.frase_furigana: この 町[まち]には魅力[みりょく]があります。
vc141fa938a.frase_es: This town has a lot of charm.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

vc141fa938a.matiz: 魅力[みりょく]がある = to have charm, to be appealing. 魅力的[みりょくてき]な = attractive, charming.

v052ee6aa11.frase_furigana: この 前[まえ]、 先輩[せんぱい]に 会[あ]ったよ。
v052ee6aa11.frase_es: I ran into one of my seniors the other day.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
に: destination, time, where something is

v052ee6aa11.matiz: この前[まえ] looks back at the recent past; 今度[こんど] looks ahead to the near future.

v6d7781cd19.frase: 彼らは最後まで戦いました。
v6d7781cd19.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]らは 最後[さいご]まで戦[たたか]いました。
v6d7781cd19.tono: タタカウ
v6d7781cd19.frase_es: They fought to the very end.
v6d7781cd19.matiz: Fighting in a war, a match or against a hardship. The opponent takes と: 病気[びょうき]と戦[たたか]う = to fight an illness.

va42e84b222.frase: ニャンはスーパーでおにぎりを見てるよ。
va42e84b222.frase_furigana: ニャンはスーパーでおにぎりを 見[み]てるよ。
va42e84b222.frase_es: Nyan is looking at the onigiri at the supermarket.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v8c02a3756d.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]のお 願[ねが]い、断[ことわ]ったよ。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v8c02a3756d.matiz: To turn down an invitation or a request, usually politely.

vae1474fe4a.frase: ニャンは食べすぎて、体重が増えたよ。
vae1474fe4a.frase_furigana: ニャンは 食[た]べすぎて、体重[たいじゅう]が 増[ふ]えたよ。
vae1474fe4a.tono: タイジュウ
vae1474fe4a.frase_es: Nyan ate too much and gained weight.

gramatica.nota: 食べすぎる = to eat too much: 〜すぎる after a verb stem means “too much”.

vae1474fe4a.matiz: 体重[たいじゅう]が増[ふ]える / 減[へ]る = to gain or lose weight. The weight of an object is 重[おも]さ.

v709b4c4135.frase: 世界の平和を望んでいます。
v709b4c4135.frase_furigana: 世界[せかい]の平和[へいわ]を 望[のぞ]んでいます。

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

v709b4c4135.matiz: 世界[せかい]平和[へいわ] = world peace. 平和[へいわ]な also describes a calm, peaceful life: 平和[へいわ]な毎日[まいにち].

v4124c69941.frase: 平均して一日八時間働きます。
v4124c69941.frase_furigana: 平均[へいきん]して 一日[いちにち] 八[はち] 時間[じかん] 働[はたら]きます。
v4124c69941.tono: ヘイキン
v4124c69941.frase_es: On average, I work eight hours a day.
v4124c69941.matiz: 平均[へいきん]して = on average. 平均的[へいきんてき]な = typical, ordinary, like “average” in “the average family”.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v644307beb0.matiz: An electric bell or buzzer, or a bicycle bell. A big temple bell is 鐘[かね].

v9ac84f46d9.frase_furigana: 困難[こんなん]な 状況[じょうきょう]で 頑張[がんば]ります。
v9ac84f46d9.frase_es: I'll do my best in this tough situation.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v9ac84f46d9.matiz: More formal than 難[むずか]しい, a bit like “hardship” next to “hard”: 困難[こんなん]な状況[じょうきょう] = a difficult situation.

v69097659cb.frase_es: May I ask who you are?
v69097659cb.matiz: The polite version of 誰[だれ]: どなたですか is much more courteous than 誰[だれ]ですか.

vd3e02832d8.frase: 昔、この国に王がいたよ。
vd3e02832d8.frase_furigana: 昔[むかし]、この 国[くに]に王[おう]がいたよ。
vd3e02832d8.frase_es: Long ago, this country had a king.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

vd3e02832d8.matiz: 王様[おうさま] is the friendlier, storybook word, like “the King” in fairy tales. A queen is 女王[じょおう].

v3de4792141.frase: ニャンはおもちゃで遊んでるよ。
v3de4792141.frase_furigana: ニャンはおもちゃで 遊[あそ]んでるよ。
v3de4792141.frase_es: Nyan is playing with a toy.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v98e2e631a7.frase_furigana: 彼女[かのじょ]、 学校[がっこう]の教師[きょうし]だよ。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v98e2e631a7.matiz: More formal and job-like than 先生[せんせい], which is what you call a teacher to their face. You'd write 教師 on a form, but you'd never address someone as 教師.

vd1221e42d4.frase: 安定した仕事を探しています。
vd1221e42d4.frase_furigana: 安定[あんてい]した 仕事[しごと]を 探[さが]しています。
vd1221e42d4.tono: アンテイ
vd1221e42d4.frase_es: I'm looking for a stable job.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

vd1221e42d4.matiz: 安定[あんてい]する = to become stable, to settle down. 安定[あんてい]した仕事[しごと] = a stable, secure job.

v851c239851.frase: ニャンは道でおにぎりを拾ったよ。
v851c239851.frase_furigana: ニャンは 道[みち]でおにぎりを拾[ひろ]ったよ。
alt: to pick up off the ground
v851c239851.frase_es: Nyan found an onigiri on the street.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v851c239851.matiz: To pick something up off the ground: ゴミを拾[ひろ]う = to pick up litter; お金[かね]を拾[ひろ]う = to find money lying around. Picking someone up in a car is different: 迎[むか]えに行[い]く.

v6ba761fb67.frase: 今年の目標を立てました。
v6ba761fb67.frase_furigana: 今年[ことし]の目標[もくひょう]を 立[た]てました。
v6ba761fb67.tono: モクヒョウ
v6ba761fb67.frase_es: I set my goals for this year.
v6ba761fb67.matiz: 目標[もくひょう]を立[た]てる = to set a goal.

v8c2790749a.frase: これはまさに私が欲しかったものです。
v8c2790749a.frase_furigana: これはまさに 私[わたし]が 欲[ほ]しかったものです。
v8c2790749a.frase_es: This is exactly what I wanted.

gramatica.titulo: Generic nouns: こと, ところ, もの

v8c2790749a.matiz: Stresses that something is exactly so, like “precisely” or “truly”: まさにその通[とお]りです = that's exactly right. It sounds a little formal.

v9b23dd2bff.frase_furigana: 鼻[はな]が詰[つ]まってるよ。
v9b23dd2bff.frase_es: My nose is all stuffed up.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v9b23dd2bff.matiz: A pipe or your nose gets blocked: 鼻[はな]が詰[つ]まる = to have a stuffy nose. It also means “to be packed full”: 予定[よてい]が詰[つ]まっている = my schedule is packed.

vc9d2201c1d.frase: その映画にとても感動したよ。
vc9d2201c1d.frase_furigana: その 映画[えいが]にとても感動[かんどう]したよ。
vc9d2201c1d.tono: カンドウ

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
に: destination, time, where something is

vc9d2201c1d.matiz: 感動[かんどう]する = to be moved, to be touched. What moves you takes に: 映画[えいが]に感動[かんどう]する. English says “it moved me”; Japanese says “I was moved by it”.

v5008ea5db7.frase_furigana: 部屋[へや]を 花[はな]で飾[かざ]ったよ。
v5008ea5db7.frase_es: I decorated my room with flowers.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v5008ea5db7.matiz: To decorate a room or a table: 花[はな]を飾[かざ]る = to put out flowers as decoration. Also for putting something on display: 写真[しゃしん]を飾[かざ]る = to put up a photo.

vf782eb1b65.frase: 暗い部屋でニャンの目が光るよ。
vf782eb1b65.frase_furigana: 暗[くら]い 部屋[へや]でニャンの 目[め]が光[ひか]るよ。
vf782eb1b65.frase_es: Nyan's eyes glow in the dark room.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
で: where an action happens / with what

vf782eb1b65.matiz: Intransitive: a light or an object gives off light: 星[ほし]が光[ひか]る = the stars shine.

v12badcfbf7.frase: 重い荷物で腰が痛いです。
v12badcfbf7.frase_furigana: 重[おも]い 荷物[にもつ]で腰[こし]が 痛[いた]いです。
v12badcfbf7.frase_es: My lower back hurts from carrying heavy stuff.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v12badcfbf7.matiz: 腰[こし]が痛[いた]い is the usual way to say “my back hurts” after lifting something heavy. In a broader sense it also covers the hips and waist.

v77987ae703.frase: 手紙を封筒に入れました。
v77987ae703.frase_furigana: 手紙[てがみ]を封筒[ふうとう]に 入[い]れました。
v77987ae703.tono: フウトウ
v77987ae703.frase_es: I put the letter in the envelope.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v4ad8b6c437.frase: 車のシートを新しくしました。
v4ad8b6c437.frase_furigana: 車[くるま]のシートを 新[あたら]しくしました。
v4ad8b6c437.frase_es: I got new seats for my car.
v4ad8b6c437.matiz: Two different English words share this katakana: a seat (車[くるま]のシート = a car seat) or a sheet of material (プラスチックのシート = a plastic sheet).

vf00ce5f0aa.frase: 子供の背、ずいぶん伸びたよ。
vf00ce5f0aa.frase_furigana: 子供[こども]の 背[せ]、ずいぶん伸[の]びたよ。
vf00ce5f0aa.frase_es: The kid has really shot up.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vf00ce5f0aa.matiz: Intransitive partner of 伸[の]ばす: 髪[かみ]が伸[の]びる = your hair grows. 背[せ]が伸[の]びる = to grow taller.

v74aa260b9e.frase_furigana: 週[しゅう]に 一[いち] 度[ど]、 掃除[そうじ]をします。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v74aa260b9e.matiz: Used as a unit of time: 週[しゅう]に一度[いちど] = once a week. “A week” as a length of time is usually 一週間[いっしゅうかん].

v3a0dc2f2bc.frase_furigana: 服[ふく]に穴[あな]があります。
v3a0dc2f2bc.frase_es: There's a hole in my clothes.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v9e752b0065.frase: 駅の近くにスポーツセンターがあります。
v9e752b0065.frase_furigana: 駅[えき]の 近[ちか]くにスポーツセンターがあります。
v9e752b0065.frase_es: There's a sports center near the station.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v9e752b0065.matiz: A center as a building or facility: スポーツセンター, ショッピングセンター. For the middle of something, use 中心[ちゅうしん].

vce9e52a354.frase: いい印象を持ちました。
vce9e52a354.frase_furigana: いい印象[いんしょう]を 持[も]ちました。
vce9e52a354.tono: インショウ
vce9e52a354.frase_es: I came away with a good impression.
vce9e52a354.matiz: 第一[だいいち]印象[いんしょう] = first impression. いい印象[いんしょう]を持[も]つ = to have a good impression of something.

v87dfd277b6.frase: 彼女は病院の医師です。
v87dfd277b6.frase_furigana: 彼女[かのじょ]は 病院[びょういん]の医師[いし]です。
v87dfd277b6.frase_es: She's a doctor at the hospital.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v87dfd277b6.matiz: More formal and official than 医者[いしゃ], the everyday word, a bit like “physician” next to “doctor”.

vfaa27922e0.frase_furigana: このファイル、 開[ひら]いて。
vfaa27922e0.matiz: A computer file, or a paper folder or binder for documents: このファイルを開[ひら]いてください = please open this file.

v820e9a070b.frase: ニャンは棚の上で寝てるよ。
v820e9a070b.frase_furigana: ニャンは棚[たな]の 上[うえ]で 寝[ね]てるよ。
v820e9a070b.frase_es: Nyan is sleeping on top of the shelf.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v820e9a070b.matiz: 本棚[ほんだな] = a bookshelf.

v78fa7f7fd3.frase: 寒いからセーター着たよ。
v78fa7f7fd3.frase_furigana: 寒[さむ]いからセーター 着[き]たよ。
v78fa7f7fd3.frase_es: It was cold, so I put on a sweater.

gramatica.titulo: から and ので: because

vf2f8dbaeff.frase: 彼はずっと黙っていました。
vf2f8dbaeff.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]はずっと黙[だま]っていました。
vf2f8dbaeff.frase_es: He kept quiet the whole time.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

vf2f8dbaeff.matiz: 黙[だま]って = silently, without a word: 黙[だま]って聞[き]く = to listen in silence. It also means “without telling anyone”: 黙[だま]って出[で]かける = to head out without a word.

vb801a17f90.frase_furigana: 先日[せんじつ]は 本当[ほんとう]にありがとう。
vb801a17f90.tono: センジツ
vb801a17f90.frase_es: Thank you so much for the other day.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is
は: the topic of the sentence

vb801a17f90.matiz: More formal than この前[まえ], and very common at the start of letters and emails. Japanese often thanks people again for a past kindness the next time they meet: 先日[せんじつ]はありがとうございました.

v07a64f1953.frase_furigana: 紅茶[こうちゃ]を 一杯[いっぱい] 飲[の]みました。
v07a64f1953.frase_es: I had a cup of black tea.
v07a64f1953.matiz: Literally “red tea”: the black tea common in the West. Japanese green tea is お茶[ちゃ] or 緑茶[りょくちゃ], and in Japan plain “tea” usually means green tea.

v425aeaca88.frase_furigana: 遠慮[えんりょ]しないで 食[た]べて。
v425aeaca88.frase_es: Don't be shy, go ahead and eat.
v425aeaca88.matiz: 遠慮[えんりょ]する = to hold back out of politeness, so as not to impose. ご遠慮[えんりょ]なく = don't be shy, help yourself. On signs, ご遠慮[えんりょ]ください politely means “please don't”.

ve355c304cb.frase: 姉が女の子を生んだよ。
ve355c304cb.frase_furigana: 姉[あね]が 女[おんな]の 子[こ]を生[う]んだよ。
ve355c304cb.frase_es: My big sister had a baby girl.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

ve355c304cb.matiz: Giving birth to a child, or producing something new: アイデアを生[う]む = to come up with an idea. Being born is 生[う]まれる.

vec2683aa5e.frase: ニャンのしっぽを踏んじゃった。
vec2683aa5e.frase_furigana: ニャンのしっぽを踏[ふ]んじゃった。
vec2683aa5e.frase_es: Oops, I stepped on Nyan's tail.

gramatica.titulo: 〜てしまう: ending up doing (by accident)

vec2683aa5e.matiz: Stepping on something, by accident or on purpose: 足[あし]を踏[ふ]む = to step on someone's foot.

v3dcfc6ae54.frase: 友達にはがきを送りました。
v3dcfc6ae54.frase_furigana: 友達[ともだち]にはがきを 送[おく]りました。
v3dcfc6ae54.frase_es: I sent a postcard to a friend.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

ve58ea47b79.frase: 山からの景色、きれいだね。
ve58ea47b79.frase_furigana: 山[やま]からの景色[けしき]、きれいだね。
ve58ea47b79.frase_es: The view from the mountain is beautiful, isn't it?

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v08fb5f6b69.frase: 手紙をポストに入れました。
v08fb5f6b69.frase_furigana: 手紙[てがみ]をポストに 入[い]れました。
v08fb5f6b69.frase_es: I put the letter in the mailbox.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v08fb5f6b69.matiz: The red mailbox on the street, for sending letters. The mailbox at your home can also be called ポスト.

v6a21638ead.frase: ニャンの噂を聞いたよ。
v6a21638ead.frase_furigana: ニャンの噂[うわさ]を 聞[き]いたよ。
v6a21638ead.frase_es: I heard a rumor about Nyan.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v6a21638ead.matiz: 噂[うわさ]をする = to talk about someone who isn't there. 噂[うわさ]をすれば… = speak of the devil…

v7eb6d36e9f.frase: 部屋に植物を置いています。
v7eb6d36e9f.frase_furigana: 部屋[へや]に植物[しょくぶつ]を 置[お]いています。
v7eb6d36e9f.frase_es: I keep plants in my room.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
に: destination, time, where something is

v7eb6d36e9f.matiz: Plants as living things, the partner word of 動物[どうぶつ] (animal). A factory “plant” is 工場[こうじょう].

vf1ca2d223d.frase: 手の感覚がありません。
vf1ca2d223d.frase_furigana: 手[て]の感覚[かんかく]がありません。
vf1ca2d223d.tono: カンカク

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

vf1ca2d223d.matiz: 五感[ごかん] = the five senses. 感覚[かんかく]がない = to have no feeling, to be numb.

v97fba0da8e.frase: 日本語の勉強で苦労してるよ。
v97fba0da8e.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]の 勉強[べんきょう]で苦労[くろう]してるよ。
v97fba0da8e.frase_es: I'm having a hard time studying Japanese.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v97fba0da8e.matiz: 苦労[くろう]する = to struggle, to have a hard time with something.

vc8ca5b1b20.frase: 若者たちは音楽が好きです。
vc8ca5b1b20.frase_furigana: 若者[わかもの]たちは 音楽[おんがく]が 好[す]きです。
vc8ca5b1b20.tono: ワカモノ

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Liking and being good at: が with adjectives

vc8ca5b1b20.matiz: 若[わか]い (young) + 者[もの] (person). Often means young people as a group, like “the youth of today”: 最近[さいきん]の若者[わかもの].

v45d2501d2b.frase: 天気の話題から始めようよ。
v45d2501d2b.frase_furigana: 天気[てんき]の話題[わだい]から 始[はじ]めようよ。
v45d2501d2b.frase_es: Let's start by talking about the weather.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v45d2501d2b.matiz: 話題[わだい]にする = to bring something up in conversation; 話題[わだい]を変[か]える = to change the subject. 話題[わだい]の映画[えいが] = the movie everyone's talking about.

v62747c1e33.frase: 父はいつもネクタイをしています。
v62747c1e33.frase_furigana: 父[ちち]はいつもネクタイをしています。
v62747c1e33.frase_es: My father always wears a tie.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

vbd7b78f145.frase: ニャンは虫を捕まえようとしたよ。
vbd7b78f145.frase_furigana: ニャンは 虫[むし]を捕[つか]まえようとしたよ。
vbd7b78f145.tono: ツカマエル
vbd7b78f145.frase_es: Nyan tried to catch a bug.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vbd7b78f145.matiz: Catching something that's getting away: 泥棒[どろぼう]を捕[つか]まえる = to catch a thief. Also タクシーを捕[つか]まえる = to grab a taxi.

v222a8e536a.matiz: A traditional Japanese sliding door. An ordinary Western-style door is ドア.

v17b075aaea.frase: 髪を後ろで結びました。
v17b075aaea.frase_furigana: 髪[かみ]を 後[うし]ろで結[むす]びました。

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v17b075aaea.matiz: Tying a knot, or linking two things: 二[ふた]つの町[まち]を結[むす]ぶ = to connect two towns.

v64665351eb.frase_furigana: 田舎[いなか]で育[そだ]ちました。
v64665351eb.frase_es: I grew up in the countryside.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v64665351eb.matiz: Intransitive: a person, an animal or a plant grows up. The transitive partner is 育[そだ]てる (to raise).

vb05f9b1f48.frase: ニャンは落ちて怪我しちゃったよ。
vb05f9b1f48.frase_furigana: ニャンは 落[お]ちて怪我[けが]しちゃったよ。

gramatica.titulo: 〜てしまう: ending up doing (by accident)

vb05f9b1f48.matiz: 怪我[けが]をする = to get hurt, to be injured. Often written in kana: けが or ケガ.

vd148b934fb.frase: この町を観光しました。
vd148b934fb.frase_furigana: この 町[まち]を観光[かんこう]しました。
vd148b934fb.tono: カンコウ
vd148b934fb.frase_es: I went sightseeing around this town.
vd148b934fb.matiz: 観光[かんこう]する = to go sightseeing. 観光地[かんこうち] = a tourist spot; 観光客[かんこうきゃく] = a tourist.

vf996180809.frase: 店は九時に閉まります。
vf996180809.frase_furigana: 店[みせ]は 九[く] 時[じ]に閉[し]まります。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vf996180809.matiz: Intransitive: a door or a shop closes. The transitive partner is 閉[し]める (to close something). English uses “close” for both.

v04711658ee.frase_furigana: 雪[ゆき]で 道[みち]が滑[すべ]ります。
v04711658ee.frase_es: The roads are slippery with snow.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v04711658ee.matiz: Slipping and losing your balance, or gliding smoothly: 雪[ゆき]で滑[すべ]る = to slip on the snow. Skiing and skating are 滑る too.

v0816b1d2eb.frase: ニャンの手が汚れてるよ。
v0816b1d2eb.frase_furigana: ニャンの 手[て]が汚[よご]れてるよ。
v0816b1d2eb.tono: ヨゴレル

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v0816b1d2eb.matiz: Intransitive: clothes get dirty. The transitive partner is 汚[よご]す (to make something dirty). 汚[よご]れている = to be dirty.

v32d1172b38.frase: これは二人だけの秘密だよ。
v32d1172b38.frase_furigana: これは 二人[ふたり]だけの秘密[ひみつ]だよ。
v32d1172b38.frase_es: This is just between the two of us.

gramatica.titulo: Only: だけ, しか, ばかり
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v32d1172b38.matiz: 秘密[ひみつ]にする = to keep something secret; 秘密[ひみつ]を守[まも]る = to keep a secret.

v00c764f80c.frase_furigana: 計画[けいかく]を進[すす]めようよ。
v00c764f80c.tono: ススメル
v00c764f80c.frase_es: Let's move ahead with the plan.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v00c764f80c.matiz: Transitive partner of 進[すす]む (to advance): 計画[けいかく]を進[すす]める = to push ahead with a plan. Don't confuse it with 勧[すす]める (to recommend), which sounds the same.

vcdcfe03e38.frase: クリスマスに何をしますか。
vcdcfe03e38.frase_furigana: クリスマスに 何[なに]をしますか。
vcdcfe03e38.frase_es: What are you doing for Christmas?

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vcdcfe03e38.matiz: In Japan it's celebrated more as a romantic or casual family occasion than a religious one. Christmas Eve is a big date night for couples.

vf7c32d5c3d.frase: 病気から回復しました。
vf7c32d5c3d.frase_furigana: 病気[びょうき]から回復[かいふく]しました。
vf7c32d5c3d.tono: カイフク
vf7c32d5c3d.matiz: 回復[かいふく]する = to recover, from an illness or a setback. It's also used for the economy or the weather picking up.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v942993662d.frase: ニャンは猫に恋してるよ。
v942993662d.frase_furigana: ニャンは 猫[ねこ]に恋[こい]してるよ。
v942993662d.frase_es: Nyan is in love with a cat.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
よ and ね at the end of a sentence
に: destination, time, where something is

v942993662d.matiz: 恋[こい]をする = to fall in love. 恋 is romantic love, often the longing kind. 愛[あい] is love in general, including for family and friends. 初恋[はつこい] = first love.

v4f8c39b31c.frase: 猫の動きはとても速いです。
v4f8c39b31c.frase_furigana: 猫[ねこ]の動[うご]きはとても 速[はや]いです。
v4f8c39b31c.matiz: The noun form of 動[うご]く: 手[て]の動[うご]き = the movement of a hand. It can also mean a trend: 市場[しじょう]の動[うご]き = market trends.

vc6cdafb772.frase_furigana: このパンは固[かた]いです。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vc6cdafb772.matiz: For solid, firm things. かたい has a few kanji: 硬[かた]い is for hard materials like stone or metal, 堅[かた]い for something solid and steady. It can describe people too: 頭[あたま]が固[かた]い = stubborn, inflexible.

v829e33739c.frase_furigana: 荷物[にもつ]を届[とど]けました。
v829e33739c.matiz: Taking something all the way to where it should go: 荷物[にもつ]を届[とど]ける = to deliver a package. The intransitive partner is 届[とど]く (to arrive, to reach).

v8c4e377625.frase: ニャンが起きた瞬間、雨が降り始めたよ。
v8c4e377625.frase_furigana: ニャンが 起[お]きた瞬間[しゅんかん]、 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]り 始[はじ]めたよ。
v8c4e377625.tono: シュンカン
v8c4e377625.frase_es: The moment Nyan woke up, it started raining.

gramatica.nota: 降り始める: 始める after a verb's ます-stem means “to start to”. 降り始めた = “it started raining”.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v8c4e377625.matiz: その瞬間[しゅんかん] = at that very instant. After a past verb: 見[み]た瞬間[しゅんかん] = the moment I saw it.

v60bcc6ce97.frase_furigana: 眼鏡[めがね]を外[はず]して 寝[ね]たよ。
v60bcc6ce97.frase_es: I took off my glasses and went to sleep.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v60bcc6ce97.matiz: Taking off something worn or attached: 眼鏡[めがね]を外[はず]す = to take off your glasses. For clothes and shoes, use 脱[ぬ]ぐ instead.

v6dd67860f3.frase: ここでタバコは禁止です。
v6dd67860f3.frase_furigana: ここでタバコは禁止[きんし]です。

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
は: the topic of the sentence

v6dd67860f3.matiz: 禁止[きんし]する = to ban, to forbid. You'll see it on signs: 駐車[ちゅうしゃ]禁止[きんし] = no parking.

vcaa6e7803a.frase: ニャンは箸が使えないよ。
vcaa6e7803a.frase_furigana: ニャンは箸[はし]が 使[つか]えないよ。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

vcaa6e7803a.matiz: Don't confuse it with 橋[はし] (bridge): same reading, different kanji. Often said politely as お箸[はし].

v307feb83e9.frase: お正月に家族と会います。
v307feb83e9.frase_furigana: お正月[しょうがつ]に 家族[かぞく]と 会[あ]います。
v307feb83e9.tono: ショウガツ
v307feb83e9.frase_es: I see my family over New Year's.

gramatica.titulo: と and や: lists of things
に: destination, time, where something is

v307feb83e9.matiz: Usually said with お: お正月[しょうがつ]. It's the biggest holiday of the year in Japan, the first days of January spent with family.

v5e35d5681f.frase: 来月、友達の結婚式があるよ。
v5e35d5681f.frase_furigana: 来月[らいげつ]、 友達[ともだち]の結婚[けっこん] 式[しき]があるよ。
v5e35d5681f.tono: ケッコンシキ
v5e35d5681f.frase_es: My friend's wedding is next month.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v5e35d5681f.matiz: 結婚[けっこん] (marriage) + 式[しき] (ceremony).

vbac4b796d0.frase_furigana: このキーを 押[お]して。
vbac4b796d0.matiz: A key on a keyboard. A key for a lock is usually 鍵[かぎ].

v0997a9151b.frase: ニャンはいつも私を無視するよ。
v0997a9151b.frase_furigana: ニャンはいつも 私[わたし]を無視[むし]するよ。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v0997a9151b.matiz: 無視[むし]する = to ignore on purpose. Don't confuse it with 虫[むし] (bug), which sounds the same. 信号[しんごう]無視[むし] = running a red light.

vcdd8d973c4.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]は優[すぐ]れた 選手[せんしゅ]です。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

vcdd8d973c4.matiz: Almost always used as 優[すぐ]れた + noun, or 優[すぐ]れている: 優[すぐ]れた選手[せんしゅ] = an excellent player.

ve42c4ae905.frase: その説明に疑問があります。
ve42c4ae905.frase_furigana: その 説明[せつめい]に疑問[ぎもん]があります。
ve42c4ae905.frase_es: I have some doubts about that explanation.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

ve42c4ae905.matiz: A doubt or open question in your mind, not one you ask out loud (that's 質問[しつもん]). 疑問[ぎもん]に思[おも]う = to have doubts about something, to wonder.

v3408f29b99.frase: 彼はとても熱心な学生です。
v3408f29b99.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]はとても熱心[ねっしん]な 学生[がくせい]です。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v3408f29b99.matiz: 熱心[ねっしん]な学生[がくせい] = a hardworking, eager student. 熱心[ねっしん]に = eagerly: 熱心[ねっしん]に勉強[べんきょう]する = to study hard. Literally “hot heart”.

vea632a9c2a.frase_furigana: 暑[あつ]くて汗[あせ]が 出[で]ました。
vea632a9c2a.frase_es: It was hot, and I was sweating.
vea632a9c2a.matiz: 汗[あせ]が出[で]る or 汗[あせ]をかく = to sweat. Japanese uses the noun where English just says “sweat” as a verb.

v15e758fb52.frase: 料理の材料を買いました。
v15e758fb52.frase_furigana: 料理[りょうり]の材料[ざいりょう]を 買[か]いました。
v15e758fb52.frase_es: I bought the ingredients for cooking.
v15e758fb52.matiz: Ingredients for cooking, or materials for making something: 材料[ざいりょう]を買[か]う = to buy the ingredients.

v05a60af8ed.frase: 熱いスープを飲みました。
v05a60af8ed.frase_furigana: 熱[あつ]いスープを 飲[の]みました。
v05a60af8ed.matiz: Western-style soup. Japanese soups, like miso soup, are usually called 汁[しる] or 汁物[しるもの]. Note that you drink soup in Japanese: スープを飲[の]む.

v2b7d7b5bf6.frase: この映画は日本で撮影されました。
v2b7d7b5bf6.frase_furigana: この 映画[えいが]は 日本[にほん]で撮影[さつえい]されました。
v2b7d7b5bf6.tono: サツエイ
v2b7d7b5bf6.frase_es: This movie was filmed in Japan.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v2b7d7b5bf6.matiz: 撮影[さつえい]する = to film or to photograph, sounding more professional than 撮[と]る. 撮影[さつえい]禁止[きんし] = no photography.

va25c5224c9.frase_furigana: 収入[しゅうにゅう]が 少[すく]ないよ。
va25c5224c9.tono: シュウニュウ

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

va25c5224c9.matiz: The opposite is 支出[ししゅつ] (expenses).

va68fcf4e26.frase_furigana: 中央[ちゅうおう]に 立[た]ってください。
va68fcf4e26.tono: チュウオウ

gramatica.titulo: Asking for things: ください
に: destination, time, where something is

va68fcf4e26.matiz: The middle point of something. For the center of a city or of attention, 中心[ちゅうしん] is common too. 中央[ちゅうおう]銀行[ぎんこう] = central bank.

v725a7278f1.frase: とうとう雨が降ってきたよ。
v725a7278f1.frase_furigana: とうとう 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]ってきたよ。
v725a7278f1.tono: トウトウ

gramatica.titulo: 〜ていく and 〜てくる: direction in time

v725a7278f1.matiz: Like やっと, but とうとう often has a resigned or negative feel, “it finally happened”: とうとう雨[あめ]が降[ふ]った. やっと is for things you're relieved to see happen.

v6e039723fd.frase_furigana: 公園[こうえん]の桜[さくら]、きれいだね。
v6e039723fd.frase_es: The cherry blossoms in the park are beautiful, aren't they?

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v6e039723fd.matiz: 桜[さくら]が咲[さ]く = the cherry blossoms bloom, the symbol of spring in Japan. Going out to enjoy them, often with a picnic, is お花見[はなみ].

ve23cfdc92c.frase: ニャンは砂の上で寝てるよ。
ve23cfdc92c.frase_furigana: ニャンは砂[すな]の 上[うえ]で 寝[ね]てるよ。
ve23cfdc92c.frase_es: Nyan is sleeping on the sand.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v4ec14da9b0.frase_furigana: 昨夜[さくや]はよく 眠[ねむ]れました。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v4ec14da9b0.matiz: More formal than 昨日[きのう]の夜[よる]. In everyday speech you'll also hear ゆうべ.

v94dac2199a.frase: 将来のことで悩んでるよ。
v94dac2199a.frase_furigana: 将来[しょうらい]のことで悩[なや]んでるよ。

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v94dac2199a.matiz: Agonizing over a problem, torn about what to do: 将来[しょうらい]のことで悩[なや]む. It's deeper and longer-lasting than 心配[しんぱい]する. 悩[なや]み = a worry, a problem.

v3f42ed92c4.frase: 歴史に関心があります。
v3f42ed92c4.frase_furigana: 歴史[れきし]に関心[かんしん]があります。
v3f42ed92c4.tono: カンシン

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v3f42ed92c4.matiz: 関心[かんしん]がある = to take an interest in something, a little more serious than 興味[きょうみ]. Don't confuse it with 感心[かんしん] (admiration), which sounds the same.

v4d89dcfa76.frase: 試験の前は緊張するよ。
v4d89dcfa76.frase_furigana: 試験[しけん]の 前[まえ]は緊張[きんちょう]するよ。
v4d89dcfa76.tono: キンチョウ

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v4d89dcfa76.matiz: 緊張[きんちょう]する = to get nervous, to tense up.

v29152ce7e7.frase: 友達を映画に誘ったよ。
v29152ce7e7.frase_furigana: 友達[ともだち]を 映画[えいが]に誘[さそ]ったよ。
v29152ce7e7.frase_es: I asked a friend to the movies.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
に: destination, time, where something is

v29152ce7e7.matiz: Inviting someone to do something together: 映画[えいが]に誘[さそ]う = to ask someone to the movies. A formal invitation, like to a wedding, is 招待[しょうたい].

vfec668ca83.frase: 電車以外の手段がありません。
vfec668ca83.frase_furigana: 電車[でんしゃ] 以外[いがい]の手段[しゅだん]がありません。
vfec668ca83.frase_es: The train is the only way to get there.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)

vfec668ca83.matiz: 交通[こうつう]手段[しゅだん] = means of transportation. 手段[しゅだん]を選[えら]ばない = to stop at nothing.

va17021d336.frase_furigana: 車[くるま]が故障[こしょう]しました。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

va17021d336.matiz: 故障[こしょう]する = for a machine to break down. On a sign, 故障中[こしょうちゅう] = out of order.

v0cb9436c19.frase_furigana: 発音[はつおん]が 難[むずか]しいです。
v0cb9436c19.tono: ハツオン

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v0cb9436c19.matiz: 発音[はつおん]する = to pronounce.

vbf6ea49a94.frase_furigana: この糸[いと]、 細[ほそ]いね。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v12ab5d5444.frase_furigana: 生命[せいめい]は 大切[たいせつ]です。

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v12ab5d5444.matiz: More formal and scientific than 命[いのち]: 生命[せいめい]保険[ほけん] = life insurance. Your daily life is 生活[せいかつ].

v2044bfe6b4.frase: ニャンが走ると、床が揺れます。
v2044bfe6b4.frase_furigana: ニャンが 走[はし]ると、 床[ゆか]が揺[ゆ]れます。
v2044bfe6b4.frase_es: When Nyan runs, the floor shakes.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v2044bfe6b4.matiz: Intransitive: the ground, a tree or a boat shakes or sways by itself: 地震[じしん]で家[いえ]が揺[ゆ]れる = the house shakes in an earthquake.

v82f2f466f5.frase: ニャンのおもちゃの糸が切れました。
v82f2f466f5.frase_furigana: ニャンのおもちゃの 糸[いと]が切[き]れました。
v82f2f466f5.frase_es: The string on Nyan's toy snapped.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

v82f2f466f5.matiz: Intransitive: a string snaps by itself, or something runs out: 電池[でんち]が切[き]れる = the battery dies. In slang, キレる = to snap, to lose your temper.

v03b76e3a2d.frase: ニャンは傘を差して出かけました。
v03b76e3a2d.frase_furigana: ニャンは 傘[かさ]を差[さ]して 出[で]かけました。
v03b76e3a2d.frase_es: Nyan put up his umbrella and went out.
v03b76e3a2d.matiz: 傘[かさ]を差[さ]す = to open or hold up an umbrella, where English just says “use an umbrella”. Light can 差す too: 日[ひ]が差[さ]す = the sun shines in.

v8d1341e74e.frase_furigana: 夢[ゆめ]を抱[いだ]いています。
v8d1341e74e.frase_es: I hold a dream in my heart.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

v8d1341e74e.matiz: Formal, for feelings and hopes: 疑問[ぎもん]を抱[いだ]く = to have doubts; 夢[ゆめ]を抱[いだ]く = to cherish a dream. Read だく, the same kanji means holding someone in your arms.

vc3a9d787a1.frase: ニャンはおもちゃを戻しませんでした。
vc3a9d787a1.frase_furigana: ニャンはおもちゃを戻[もど]しませんでした。
vc3a9d787a1.frase_es: Nyan didn't put the toy back.
vc3a9d787a1.matiz: Transitive partner of 戻[もど]る (to come back): 本[ほん]を棚[たな]に戻[もど]す = to put a book back on the shelf.

v300ea1a34b.frase: この辺に郵便局はありますか。
v300ea1a34b.frase_furigana: この 辺[へん]に 郵便[ゆうびん] 局[きょく]はありますか。
v300ea1a34b.frase_es: Is there a post office around here?

gramatica.titulo: Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v300ea1a34b.matiz: Handy for asking directions: この辺[へん]に〜はありますか = is there a … around here? It also means “at this point”: 今日[きょう]はこの辺[へん]で = let's stop here for today.

v78d8189df4.frase: みんなの意見を受け入れることにしたよ。
v78d8189df4.frase_furigana: みんなの 意見[いけん]を受[う]け 入[い]れることにしたよ。
v78d8189df4.tono: ウケイレル
v78d8189df4.frase_es: I decided to go along with what everyone thought.

gramatica.nota: 〜ことにする: deciding to do something, by your own choice. 受け入れることにした = “I decided to accept”.

gramatica.titulo: Relative clauses (a sentence describes a noun)

v78d8189df4.matiz: Accepting an idea, a person or a situation: 意見[いけん]を受[う]け入[い]れる = to accept someone's opinion.

v4f80787622.frase: ニャンは湖の魚を見ています。
v4f80787622.frase_furigana: ニャンは湖[みずうみ]の 魚[さかな]を 見[み]ています。
v4f80787622.frase_es: Nyan is watching the fish in the lake.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

v6f62c4abf4.frase: ニャンの話を聞いて、「なるほど」と思いました。
v6f62c4abf4.frase_furigana: ニャンの 話[はなし]を 聞[き]いて、「なるほど」と 思[おも]いました。
v6f62c4abf4.tono: ナルホド
v6f62c4abf4.frase_es: When I heard what Nyan said, I thought, “Ah, that makes sense.”
v6f62c4abf4.matiz: Shows that you've understood, or that you agree with what you've just been told. Careful with people above you: saying なるほど to your boss can sound like you're judging what they said.

v83fa4b6289.frase: 山を越えて村に着いたよ。
v83fa4b6289.frase_furigana: 山[やま]を越[こ]えて 村[むら]に 着[つ]いたよ。
v83fa4b6289.frase_es: I crossed the mountain and reached the village.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v83fa4b6289.matiz: Crossing over a border or a mountain: 山[やま]を越[こ]える. With numbers it means to go over, often written 超[こ]える: 100人[にん]を超[こ]える = more than 100 people.

vc4103593c6.frase_furigana: おばあちゃん、 遊[あそ]びに 来[き]て。
vc4103593c6.tono: オバアチャン

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vc4103593c6.matiz: Affectionate and casual, for calling your own grandma. The more neutral form is おばあさん.

v6f301e6054.frase: ニャンは大きい声で叫びました。
v6f301e6054.frase_furigana: ニャンは 大[おお]きい 声[こえ]で叫[さけ]びました。
v6f301e6054.frase_es: Nyan shouted at the top of his voice.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

vc28461a451.frase: ニャンはますます眠くなりました。
vc28461a451.frase_furigana: ニャンはますます 眠[ねむ]くなりました。
vc28461a451.matiz: Stresses a change that keeps growing: 雨[あめ]がますます強[つよ]くなる = the rain keeps getting heavier. English often doubles the adjective instead: “heavier and heavier”.

v651b2029d7.frase: ニャンには変な癖があります。
v651b2029d7.frase_furigana: ニャンには 変[へん]な癖[くせ]があります。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v651b2029d7.matiz: A personal habit or quirk, often a bad one: 癖[くせ]がある = to have a habit. 口癖[くちぐせ] = a pet phrase, something you're always saying. Good daily routines are 習慣[しゅうかん].

v8f614fd19f.frase: このベッドは柔らかいです。
v8f614fd19f.frase_furigana: このベッドは柔[やわ]らかいです。
v8f614fd19f.tono: ヤワラカイ

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v8f614fd19f.matiz: The opposite of 固[かた]い. It can describe people too: 頭[あたま]が柔[やわ]らかい = open-minded, flexible.

v63ef2f385e.frase: 友達とサッカーをしたよ。
v63ef2f385e.frase_furigana: 友達[ともだち]とサッカーをしたよ。
v63ef2f385e.frase_es: I played soccer with a friend.

gramatica.titulo: と and や: lists of things
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vd3411238d7.frase_furigana: お 湯[ゆ]が沸[わ]きました。

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)

vd3411238d7.matiz: Intransitive: water boils by itself. The transitive partner is 沸[わ]かす (to boil something). Japanese says お湯[ゆ]が沸[わ]く, “the hot water boils”, even though it started out cold. お風呂[ふろ]が沸[わ]いた = the bath is ready.

vf2b97a075a.frase: 頑張ったのに、意外な結果になったよ。
vf2b97a075a.frase_furigana: 頑張[がんば]ったのに、意外[いがい]な 結果[けっか]になったよ。
vf2b97a075a.frase_es: I worked so hard, and yet the result wasn't what I expected.

gramatica.nota: 〜のに: “even though”, with a touch of frustration or surprise. 頑張ったのに = “even though I worked so hard”.

gramatica.titulo: になる (to become) and にする (to decide, to make)

vf2b97a075a.matiz: 意外[いがい]な結果[けっか] = an unexpected result. 意外[いがい]に or 意外[いがい]と = surprisingly: 意外[いがい]とおいしい = surprisingly tasty.

v35b63c5278.frase: ニャンの表情はいつも同じです。
v35b63c5278.frase_furigana: ニャンの表情[ひょうじょう]はいつも 同[おな]じです。
v35b63c5278.tono: ヒョウジョウ
v35b63c5278.frase_es: Nyan always has the same look on his face.
v35b63c5278.matiz: 彼[かれ]の表情[ひょうじょう]を見[み]て、すぐわかりました = I could tell right away from the look on his face.

v38e3d032aa.frase: ニャンは猫と喧嘩をしました。
v38e3d032aa.frase_furigana: ニャンは 猫[ねこ]と喧嘩[けんか]をしました。
v38e3d032aa.frase_es: Nyan got into a fight with another cat.

gramatica.titulo: と and や: lists of things

v38e3d032aa.matiz: 喧嘩[けんか]する = to fight or argue with someone. It covers both a shouting match and a scuffle. Often written in kana: けんか.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v9169ecb33f.frase: チームのメンバーを紹介します。
v9169ecb33f.frase_furigana: チームのメンバーを 紹介[しょうかい]します。
v9169ecb33f.frase_es: Let me introduce the members of the team.

v82bf539f6a.frase: この店は静かだし、雰囲気もいいよ。
v82bf539f6a.frase_furigana: この 店[みせ]は 静[しず]かだし、雰囲気[ふんいき]もいいよ。
v82bf539f6a.frase_es: This place is quiet, and it has a nice atmosphere too.

gramatica.nota: 〜し: listing reasons one after another, with more left unsaid. 静かだし = “it's quiet, and…”.

v82bf539f6a.matiz: The feel of a place or a situation: いい雰囲気[ふんいき]の店[みせ] = a place with a nice vibe.

v82670f1cf0.frase: 二人は手をつないで歩いたよ。
v82670f1cf0.frase_furigana: 二人[ふたり]は 手[て]をつないで 歩[ある]いたよ。
v82670f1cf0.frase_es: The two of them walked hand in hand.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v82670f1cf0.matiz: Transitive partner of つながる: 手[て]をつなぐ = to hold hands. Also for plugging things in: パソコンをネットにつなぐ = to connect a computer to the internet.

v5a330d1fa1.frase_furigana: ネットで 調[しら]べたよ。

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v5a330d1fa1.matiz: Short for インターネット, and much more common in everyday speech. ネットで = online.

v70a9c54681.frase: ニャンの毛はとても柔らかいです。
v70a9c54681.frase_furigana: ニャンの毛[け]はとても 柔[やわ]らかいです。
v70a9c54681.matiz: Body hair or an animal's fur. The hair on your head is 髪[かみ] or 髪[かみ]の毛[け]. It also means wool: 毛[け]のセーター = a wool sweater. English “hair” covers more than 毛 does.

v8159e032f2.frase: なるべくニャンを起こさないで。
v8159e032f2.frase_furigana: なるべくニャンを 起[お]こさないで。
v8159e032f2.tono: ナルベク
v8159e032f2.frase_es: Try not to wake Nyan if you can help it.
v8159e032f2.matiz: Close to できるだけ: なるべく早[はや]く来[き]てください = please come as soon as you can.

v8b9bf29837.frase: ニャンは迷惑をかけてるよ。
v8b9bf29837.frase_furigana: ニャンは迷惑[めいわく]をかけてるよ。
v8b9bf29837.frase_es: Nyan is making a nuisance of himself.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v8b9bf29837.matiz: 迷惑[めいわく]をかける = to cause someone trouble. Not bothering others matters a lot in Japan, so you'll often hear ご迷惑[めいわく]をおかけしました: sorry for the trouble.

v51cf4006b5.frase_furigana: 中学[ちゅうがく]で 英語[えいご]を 習[なら]いました。
v51cf4006b5.frase_es: I learned English in junior high.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what

v51cf4006b5.matiz: Short for 中学校[ちゅうがっこう], and very common. It covers ages 12 to 15, like American middle school. 中学生[ちゅうがくせい] = a junior high student.

v9039f3b3ea.frase_furigana: 七[しち] 時[じ]に帰宅[きたく]したよ。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v9039f3b3ea.matiz: More formal than 家[いえ]に帰[かえ]る: 帰宅[きたく]する = to return home. 帰宅部[きたくぶ], “the going-home club”, is a joke name for students who don't join any after-school club.

vb37f5d654e.frase_furigana: 机[つくえ]の 上[うえ]を整理[せいり]したよ。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vb37f5d654e.matiz: 整理[せいり]する = to sort out or organize papers, ideas or a closet. 頭[あたま]を整理[せいり]する = to get your thoughts in order.

v9aabea3ca2.frase: 昼間は働きながら、勉強してるよ。
v9aabea3ca2.frase_furigana: 昼間[ひるま]は 働[はたら]きながら、 勉強[べんきょう]してるよ。
v9aabea3ca2.frase_es: During the day, I study while I work.

gramatica.nota: 〜ながら: doing two things at once. 働きながら = “while working”.

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v9aabea3ca2.matiz: The opposite of 夜[よる]: 昼間[ひるま]は仕事[しごと]をしています = I work during the day.

vd5238fa332.frase_furigana: 数学[すうがく]が得意[とくい]だよ。

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

vd5238fa332.matiz: 得意[とくい]な科目[かもく] = your best subject. The opposite is 苦手[にがて]. 上手[じょうず] is similar but sounds like praise, so it's best for others; 得意 is fine for talking about yourself.

v475097a652.furigana: 天気予報[てんきよほう]
v475097a652.frase_furigana: 天気[てんき] 予報[よほう]を 見[み]ました。
v475097a652.tono: テンキヨホウ
v475097a652.matiz: 天気[てんき] (weather) + 予報[よほう] (forecast).

v9a94bd19a2.frase_furigana: 勇気[ゆうき]を 出[だ]して 聞[き]いたよ。
v9a94bd19a2.frase_es: I worked up the courage and asked.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v9a94bd19a2.matiz: 勇気[ゆうき]を出[だ]す = to work up the courage, literally “to put out courage”.

v92f2f34c00.frase: もっとお金を下ろせばよかったよ。
v92f2f34c00.frase_furigana: もっとお 金[かね]を下[お]ろせばよかったよ。
v92f2f34c00.frase_es: I should've taken out more money.

gramatica.nota: 〜ばよかった: “I should have…”, a regret. 下ろせばよかった = “I should have withdrawn”.

v92f2f34c00.matiz: Taking something down from a high place, or taking money out of the bank: お金[かね]を下[お]ろす = to withdraw money.

v866e1e0030.frase: ファイルを保存しました。
v866e1e0030.frase_furigana: ファイルを保存[ほぞん]しました。
v866e1e0030.matiz: 保存[ほぞん]する = to preserve food, or to save a file on a computer. Saving money is a different verb: 貯[た]める.

vffdedd167d.frase: 彼はいつもスーツを着ています。
vffdedd167d.frase_furigana: 彼[かれ]はいつもスーツを 着[き]ています。

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state

v7575f392d9.frase: 花がよく育つように、庭に植えたよ。
v7575f392d9.frase_furigana: 花[はな]がよく 育[そだ]つように、 庭[にわ]に植[う]えたよ。
v7575f392d9.frase_es: I planted the flowers in the garden so they'd grow well.

gramatica.nota: 〜ように: “so that” something happens that you can't directly control. You plant on purpose, but the growing is up to the flowers.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v7575f392d9.matiz: 庭[にわ]に木[き]を植[う]える = to plant a tree in the yard.

vde885c8eab.frase: ここに駐車してもいいですか。
vde885c8eab.frase_furigana: ここに駐車[ちゅうしゃ]してもいいですか。

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vde885c8eab.matiz: 駐車[ちゅうしゃ]する = to park. 駐車場[ちゅうしゃじょう] = a parking lot.

v16396b10bd.frase_furigana: 料金[りょうきん]を 払[はら]いました。
v16396b10bd.matiz: The charge for a service or for using something: 料金[りょうきん]を払[はら]う = to pay the fee; 電気[でんき]料金[りょうきん] = the electric bill. The price of goods in a shop is 値段[ねだん].

v026f7a3f2a.frase: 車を修理してもらいました。
v026f7a3f2a.frase_furigana: 車[くるま]を修理[しゅうり]してもらいました。

gramatica.jp: あげる・くれる・もらう

v026f7a3f2a.matiz: 修理[しゅうり]する = to repair something broken, like a machine or a car. For everyday fixing, 直[なお]す is more common.

v0da79e001e.frase: ニャンの毛がたくさん抜けるよ。
v0da79e001e.frase_furigana: ニャンの 毛[け]がたくさん抜[ぬ]けるよ。
v0da79e001e.frase_es: Nyan sheds a lot of fur.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v0da79e001e.matiz: Intransitive partner of 抜[ぬ]く: 髪[かみ]の毛[け]が抜[ぬ]ける = your hair falls out.

v0cd4c8c4ef.frase_furigana: 時間[じかん]に余裕[よゆう]があるよ。

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups
よ and ね at the end of a sentence
が: who or what (the identified subject)

v0cd4c8c4ef.matiz: 時間[じかん]に余裕[よゆう]がある = to have time to spare; 余裕[よゆう]がない = to be cutting it close. It can also mean calm confidence: 余裕[よゆう]だ = no problem, easy.

v700087d072.frase: 新しい方法を試すことができたよ。
v700087d072.frase_furigana: 新[あたら]しい 方法[ほうほう]を試[ため]すことができたよ。
v700087d072.frase_es: I got to try out a new method.

gramatica.nota: 〜ことができる: being able to do something. 試すことができた = “I was able to try it”.

gramatica.titulo: Relative clauses (a sentence describes a noun)

v700087d072.matiz: Trying something out to see if it works or if you like it: 新[あたら]しい方法[ほうほう]を試[ため]す. Trying hard, in the sense of making an effort, is 頑張[がんば]る instead.

v489b4b7cb5.frase: 勉強すればするほど、日本語のレベルが上がるよ。
v489b4b7cb5.frase_furigana: 勉強[べんきょう]すればするほど、 日本[にほん] 語[ご]のレベルが 上[あ]がるよ。
v489b4b7cb5.frase_es: The more I study, the better my Japanese gets.

gramatica.nota: 〜ば〜ほど: “the more…, the more…”. 勉強すればするほど = “the more I study”.

gramatica.titulo: Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v489b4b7cb5.matiz: A level of difficulty or skill: 日本語[にほんご]のレベルが上[あ]がりました = my Japanese level went up.

vd54313c811.frase: 学校の食堂でご飯を食べたよ。
vd54313c811.frase_furigana: 学校[がっこう]の食堂[しょくどう]でご 飯[はん]を 食[た]べたよ。
vd54313c811.tono: ショクドウ
vd54313c811.frase_es: I ate in the school cafeteria.

gramatica.titulo: で: where an action happens / with what
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vd54313c811.matiz: A school or company cafeteria. It's also a simple, casual restaurant serving set meals.

veed2e1bb5e.frase: 携帯の画面、汚れてるよ。
veed2e1bb5e.frase_furigana: 携帯[けいたい]の画面[がめん]、 汚[よご]れてるよ。

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

veed2e1bb5e.matiz: 画面[がめん]が割[わ]れる = the screen cracks.

v66215d5201.frase_furigana: 新[あたら]しい 靴[くつ]を履[は]いたよ。
v66215d5201.frase_es: I put on my new shoes.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v66215d5201.matiz: For shoes, socks, pants and skirts: anything you step into. 靴[くつ]を履[は]く. Clothes for your upper body use 着[き]る, and hats use かぶる. English “put on” or “wear” covers them all.

vfb1ffbf712.frase: この服のデザインが好きだよ。
vfb1ffbf712.frase_furigana: この 服[ふく]のデザインが 好[す]きだよ。
vfb1ffbf712.frase_es: I love the design of these clothes.

gramatica.titulo: Liking and being good at: が with adjectives
よ and ね at the end of a sentence

vfb1ffbf712.matiz: デザインする = to design.

v099780e60d.frase: 未来のことはわかりません。
v099780e60d.frase_furigana: 未来[みらい]のことはわかりません。
v099780e60d.frase_es: Nobody knows what the future holds.

gramatica.titulo: は: the topic of the sentence

v099780e60d.matiz: 未来[みらい] looks further ahead and more abstractly than 将来[しょうらい], which is your own, nearer future: 将来[しょうらい]の夢[ゆめ] = what you want to be when you grow up.

v90e28cf729.frase_furigana: あいつ、また 寝[ね]ているよ。

gramatica.titulo: 〜ている: ongoing action or resulting state
Verbs: the dictionary form and the two groups

v90e28cf729.matiz: Very casual and a bit rough; between close friends it can be playful. Like これ / それ / あれ, there's also こいつ (this guy) and そいつ (that guy there).

v0664462b5c.frase_furigana: 記念[きねん]に 写真[しゃしん]を 撮[と]りました。
v0664462b5c.frase_es: We took a photo to remember the day.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

v0664462b5c.matiz: 記念[きねん]に = as a memento, to remember the occasion. 記念日[きねんび] = anniversary; 記念[きねん]写真[しゃしん] = a souvenir photo.

v86aff1a97c.frase_furigana: 旦那[だんな]、 今[いま] 仕事[しごと] 中[ちゅう]だよ。
v86aff1a97c.frase_es: My husband's at work right now.

gramatica.titulo: よ and ね at the end of a sentence

v86aff1a97c.matiz: A casual, affectionate way to say “my husband”. The neutral word is 夫[おっと].

vcbac5a4ae6.frase: 大学の教授に相談しました。
vcbac5a4ae6.frase_furigana: 大学[だいがく]の教授[きょうじゅ]に 相談[そうだん]しました。
vcbac5a4ae6.frase_es: I asked a university professor for advice.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is

vcbac5a4ae6.matiz: A university professor, as an academic rank. To their face, students still call them 先生[せんせい], the same word used for schoolteachers.

v4635929d2e.frase_furigana: 職場[しょくば]に 友達[ともだち]がいます。
v4635929d2e.frase_es: I have a friend at work.

gramatica.titulo: が: who or what (the identified subject)
Existence: いる (living things) and ある (things)
に: destination, time, where something is

v4b6114d9e9.frase: 日本語がだいぶ上手になったよ。
v4b6114d9e9.frase_furigana: 日本[にほん] 語[ご]がだいぶ 上手[じょうず]になったよ。
v4b6114d9e9.frase_es: My Japanese has gotten a lot better.
v4b6114d9e9.matiz: Marks a noticeable change or degree: だいぶよくなりました = it's gotten much better. Also written 大分.

v9ad0c0a180.frase: この椅子は重い荷物に耐えます。
v9ad0c0a180.frase_furigana: この 椅子[いす]は 重[おも]い 荷物[にもつ]に耐[た]えます。
v9ad0c0a180.frase_es: This chair can take heavy loads.

gramatica.titulo: に: destination, time, where something is
